ISEA is committed to fostering an inclusive environment in which every individual feels respected, valued and able to contribute fully. Inclusion means actively removing barriers to participation, encouraging diverse perspectives in decision-making, and ensuring that ISEA’s culture, communications, events and digital platforms are welcoming to all.

5.3 Equity

ISEA recognises that treating all individuals identically does not always produce fair outcomes. Where appropriate and consistent with applicable law, ISEA will take proportionate steps to address disadvantage and to ensure that individuals from different backgrounds have genuinely equal access to ISEA’s opportunities, including through Reasonable Accommodation, fee concessions, mentoring and outreach initiatives referred to in Section 15.

Equal Opportunity

ISEA is committed to equal opportunity in all aspects of its activities, including membership admission, certification and examinations, committee and volunteer appointments, employment and engagement, procurement, and participation in ISEA events and professional development.

6.1 Merit-Based Decision-Making

Decisions concerning membership admission, certification, examination results, committee appointments, employment, promotion, speaking opportunities and recognition shall be based on relevant, objective and job- or role-related criteria, such as competence, qualifications, experience, conduct and performance, and shall not be influenced by any Protected Characteristic.

6.2 Equal Access

ISEA shall take reasonable steps to ensure that its membership criteria, examination arrangements, fee structures, committee selection processes and events are designed and administered in a manner that provides equal access to persons of different backgrounds, subject to Reasonable Accommodation as described in Section 11.

6.3 Positive Action

Where permitted by applicable law, ISEA may adopt proportionate positive action measures, such as targeted outreach, scholarships, mentoring programmes or diversity targets for committee composition, to address under-representation and to broaden participation in the equity research profession. Such measures are intended to expand opportunity and shall not result in the appointment or admission of a less qualified candidate over a more qualified candidate on the basis of a Protected Characteristic.

Non-Discrimination

ISEA prohibits discrimination on the basis of any Protected Characteristic in connection with its activities, including membership admission, certification, examinations, committee and volunteer appointments, employment and engagement, and participation in ISEA events.

7.1 Protected Characteristics

The Protected Characteristics recognised under this Policy include, but are not limited to, those listed in the definition of “Protected Characteristic” in Section 3. ISEA recognises that the specific characteristics protected by law vary between jurisdictions, and this Policy is intended to apply the broadest applicable protection, subject to Section 2.

7.2 Direct Discrimination

Direct discrimination occurs where a person is treated less favourably than another person is, or would be, treated in a comparable situation, because of a Protected Characteristic. Examples include declining a membership application, denying access to an examination, or excluding a person from a committee opportunity because of a Protected Characteristic rather than their qualifications or conduct.

7.3 Indirect Discrimination

Indirect discrimination occurs where an apparently neutral policy, criterion or practice disadvantages persons who share a Protected Characteristic, when compared with other persons, and cannot be objectively justified by a legitimate aim pursued by proportionate means. ISEA will keep its policies, criteria and practices under review to identify and remove any unjustified indirect discriminatory effect.

7.4 Discrimination in Membership and Certification

Membership admission, certification and examination decisions shall be made solely by reference to the criteria set out in ISEA’s Membership Policy, Membership Regulations, Member Admission Framework and applicable certification requirements. No Applicant shall be refused admission, certification or examination access because of a Protected Characteristic.

7.5 Discrimination in Employment and Engagement

ISEA is an equal opportunity employer and engager of contractors, volunteers and examiners. Recruitment, selection, remuneration, performance management, promotion, training and termination decisions shall be made on objective, role-related criteria and without regard to any Protected Characteristic, subject to and consistent with applicable local employment law.

Harassment

ISEA is committed to a professional environment free from harassment of any kind.

8.1 What Constitutes Harassment

Harassment may take many forms and may arise in any context in which individuals interact in connection with ISEA. The assessment of whether conduct constitutes harassment will have regard to the nature and circumstances of the conduct, its impact on the person concerned and all relevant circumstances, rather than solely to the intention of the person responsible.

A person’s claim that conduct was intended as a joke, criticism, expression of opinion or otherwise harmless does not, by itself, prevent the conduct from constituting harassment. Harassment may consist of a single serious incident or a pattern of behaviour, and may occur in person, in writing, electronically, or through ISEA digital platforms and social media.

Examples of conduct that may constitute harassment include, but are not limited to:

offensive, derogatory or demeaning remarks, jokes or imagery relating to a Protected Characteristic;

unwanted physical contact, or conduct of an intimidating or threatening physical nature;

displaying, circulating or posting offensive material, including online or via ISEA digital communications channels;

persistent unwanted attention, including online contact, following a request that it stop; and

mocking, mimicking or belittling a person’s accent, cultural background, disability or other Protected Characteristic.

8.2 Sexual Harassment

Sexual harassment is unwanted conduct of a sexual nature that violates a person’s dignity or creates an intimidating, hostile, degrading, humiliating or offensive environment. It may include unwelcome sexual advances, requests for sexual favours, sexually suggestive comments, jokes or imagery, and unwanted physical contact of a sexual nature. ISEA treats sexual harassment as a serious form of misconduct, particularly where it involves an actual or perceived imbalance of power or influence, such as between an examiner and a candidate, a mentor and a mentee, or a supervisor and a subordinate.

8.3 Harassment via Digital Communications and Social Media

This Policy extends to conduct on ISEA-managed digital platforms, discussion forums, virtual events and social media, and to communications made using an ISEA email address, membership designation or affiliation. Members and other persons subject to this Policy should exercise professional judgement when referencing ISEA or engaging with other Members online, and should not use such channels to harass, demean or intimidate others.

8.4 Harassment by Third Parties

ISEA will take reasonable steps to protect Members, employees, volunteers and other participants from harassment by third parties encountered in connection with ISEA activities, such as venue staff, sponsors, exhibitors or event attendees who are not themselves ISEA Members, and will address such concerns through the reporting channels described in Section 16, including, where appropriate, by engaging the relevant third-party organisation.

Bullying

ISEA does not tolerate bullying, whether or not it is related to a Protected Characteristic. Bullying is repeated, unreasonable behaviour directed at an individual or group of individuals that creates a risk to their health, safety, dignity or professional wellbeing.

Examples of conduct that may constitute bullying include, but are not limited to:

persistent, unwarranted criticism or public humiliation;

shouting, aggressive behaviour or threats;

deliberately excluding an individual from meetings, communications or professional opportunities without legitimate reason;

setting unreasonable or deliberately unachievable expectations, or withholding information necessary for an individual to perform their role or responsibilities; and

undermining an individual’s professional credibility or standing through unfounded criticism, rumour or exclusion.

ISEA distinguishes bullying from the legitimate, fair and constructive exercise of authority, such as reasonable performance management, appropriate feedback on examination or research submissions, or reasonable direction given by a committee chair, supervisor or examiner in the ordinary course of ISEA business.

Bullying can occur between peers, or can involve an actual or perceived imbalance of seniority, influence or authority, such as between a committee chair and a committee member, a senior Fellow and a Student Member, or an examiner and a candidate. ISEA treats bullying that exploits such an imbalance as a particularly serious matter. Bullying conducted through ISEA digital platforms, email or social media, including the persistent public criticism or belittling of an individual’s professional work, is treated no less seriously than bullying that occurs in person.

Victimisation

ISEA prohibits victimisation of any person because they have, in good faith:

made or supported a complaint or report under this Policy, the Whistleblower Policy or another applicable ISEA policy;

provided information or evidence in connection with an investigation or disciplinary process;

opposed conduct that they reasonably believed to be discriminatory, harassing, bullying or otherwise contrary to this Policy; or

supported another individual in raising a concern under this Policy.

Victimisation may include, but is not limited to, adverse treatment such as exclusion from committees or opportunities, unfavourable changes to responsibilities, denial of a benefit or opportunity to which the person would otherwise be entitled, or renewed harassment or bullying. Victimisation is treated by ISEA as a serious matter and may result in disciplinary action in accordance with Section 19, independently of the outcome of the underlying complaint. A complaint that is not upheld will not, of itself, be treated as having been made in bad faith, and shall not give rise to victimisation of the person who made it, provided it was made honestly and in good faith.

Accessibility and Reasonable Accommodation

ISEA is committed to ensuring that its membership, certification, governance and event processes are accessible to persons with disabilities and other individuals who may require adjustments to participate fully.

11.1 Digital Accessibility

ISEA will take reasonable steps, having regard to applicable international accessibility standards and good practice, to ensure that its website, membership portals, examination platforms and digital communications are accessible to persons with disabilities, including through compatibility with commonly used assistive technologies where reasonably practicable.

11.2 Physical Accessibility

Where ISEA organises or sanctions in-person events, examinations, conferences or chapter meetings, it will take reasonable steps to select venues that are physically accessible and to provide accessible facilities, having regard to the needs notified by attendees and the practical and financial constraints applicable to the event.

11.3 Reasonable Accommodation in Examinations and Assessment

Applicants and candidates who require Reasonable Accommodation in connection with an ISEA examination or assessment, such as extended time, accessible examination formats, a quiet testing environment, or the use of assistive technology, may request such accommodation through the process established by the relevant certification body or Executive Secretariat. Requests will be considered on an individualised basis, having regard to supporting documentation where reasonably required, the nature of the accommodation sought, and the need to maintain the integrity and validity of the assessment.

11.4 Reasonable Accommodation in Meetings and Events

Governing Council members, committee members, employees, volunteers and Members participating in ISEA meetings and events may request Reasonable Accommodation, such as accessible materials, sign language interpretation, dietary accommodation, or flexible participation arrangements including remote or hybrid attendance where feasible.

11.5 Assessing Requests

ISEA will assess each request for Reasonable Accommodation individually, in a timely and constructive manner, and in consultation with the person concerned. ISEA is not required to provide an accommodation that would impose a disproportionate or undue burden, taking into account factors such as cost, practicability, the availability of alternatives, and any impact on the integrity of an examination or assessment, but will give genuine consideration to reasonable alternatives before declining a request.

11.6 Neurodiversity, Mental Health and Wellbeing

ISEA recognises that neurodivergent individuals, and individuals experiencing mental health conditions, may benefit from Reasonable Accommodation, such as adjusted communication formats, additional processing time, or alternative meeting or examination arrangements. ISEA encourages an inclusive culture in which individuals feel able to disclose such needs in confidence, without fear of disadvantage, and will handle any disclosure in accordance with Section 22.

11.7 Language and Communication Accessibility

ISEA operates internationally and recognises that English proficiency varies across its global membership. Where reasonably practicable, ISEA will seek to make key membership, examination and governance information available in plain and clear language, and will consider requests for translation, interpretation or additional clarification in connection with ISEA processes, having regard to available resources and the need for consistency in examination administration.

Fair Treatment of Applicants and Members

ISEA is committed to ensuring that Applicants and Members are treated fairly, consistently and transparently throughout their engagement with ISEA.

12.1 Membership Admission

Membership admission decisions shall be made in accordance with the criteria and procedures set out in the Membership Policy, Membership Regulations and Member Admission Framework, applied consistently and without regard to any Protected Characteristic. Any discretionary element of the admission process shall be exercised in a manner consistent with this Policy and shall be capable of objective explanation.

12.2 Certification and Examinations

Certification and examination processes shall be administered fairly and consistently, with clear, published eligibility criteria, standardised assessment procedures, and Reasonable Accommodation available in accordance with Section 11. Examination integrity and the comparability of results across candidates shall be maintained at all times.

12.3 Committee Appointments and Volunteer Opportunities

Appointments to the Governing Council, committees and other volunteer or representative roles shall be based on relevant skills, experience, conduct and the needs of ISEA, applied through a transparent process. ISEA encourages diverse participation in its governance and committee structures, consistent with Section 6.3.

12.4 Events, Conferences and Professional Development

Access to ISEA conferences, chapter meetings, webinars, mentoring programmes and other professional development opportunities shall be offered on a fair and non-discriminatory basis, having regard to any eligibility criteria applicable to the specific opportunity, such as membership category or continuing professional development requirements.

12.5 Fair Process and Right to be Heard

Where ISEA proposes to take an adverse decision materially affecting an Applicant’s or Member’s status, such as refusal of an application, denial of an accommodation request, or a disciplinary outcome, ISEA will apply the procedural fairness safeguards set out in its Membership Regulations, Complaints Policy and Disciplinary Policy, including an appropriate opportunity for the individual to be heard, prior to a final decision being made.

Responsibilities

Upholding equality, diversity and inclusion is a shared responsibility across ISEA’s governance, staff, membership and volunteer community.

13.1 Governing Council

The Governing Council is ultimately responsible for approving this Policy, setting ISEA’s strategic direction on equality, diversity and inclusion, ensuring adequate resourcing and governance oversight, and modelling the standards of conduct expected of all persons within ISEA’s professional community.

13.2 Secretary-General and Executive Secretariat

The Secretary-General, supported by the Executive Secretariat, is responsible for the day-to-day implementation of this Policy, including embedding EDI principles into ISEA’s operational processes, membership systems, examination administration, employment practices, procurement and events, and for reporting to the Governing Council and the EDI Committee on implementation and outcomes.

13.3 Committees and Committee Chairs

Committee chairs are responsible for ensuring that committee proceedings are conducted in a manner consistent with this Policy, that committee membership and participation opportunities are offered fairly, and that any concerns raised within a committee are addressed appropriately or escalated in accordance with Section 16.

13.4 Employees, Contractors and Volunteers

Employees, contractors, examiners, assessors and volunteers acting on behalf of ISEA are responsible for conducting themselves in accordance with this Policy, completing any training required of their role, and reporting conduct that they reasonably believe to be inconsistent with this Policy.

13.5 Members

All Members are responsible for treating other Members, Applicants, ISEA staff, volunteers and third parties with dignity and respect, for complying with this Policy in all ISEA-related activities, and for cooperating reasonably with any investigation conducted under this Policy.

13.6 Chapters and Chapter Leadership

Where ISEA operates through local or regional chapters, chapter leaders are responsible for promoting and applying this Policy within their chapter’s activities, meetings and events, for escalating concerns to the Executive Secretariat or EDI Committee in accordance with Section 16, and for adapting ISEA’s EDI initiatives, where appropriate, to reflect the cultural, linguistic and legal context of the jurisdiction in which the chapter operates, without derogating from the minimum standards established by this Policy.

EDI Governance and Oversight

ISEA shall maintain an EDI Committee, reporting to the Governing Council, responsible for overseeing the implementation, monitoring and continuous improvement of this Policy.

The EDI Committee’s responsibilities may include:

advising the Governing Council on ISEA’s equality, diversity and inclusion strategy and priorities;

monitoring implementation of this Policy across ISEA’s governance, membership, certification, employment and event functions;

reviewing aggregated, anonymised diversity and inclusion data in accordance with Section 21;

recommending positive action initiatives, training programmes and outreach activities;

liaising with the Ethics & Professional Standards Committee on matters of overlap between this Policy and the Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct; and

recommending amendments to this Policy in accordance with Section 24.

The EDI Committee does not itself determine individual complaints of discrimination, harassment, bullying or victimisation; such matters are addressed through the Complaints Policy and Disciplinary Policy in accordance with Sections 16 to 19 of this Policy. The EDI Committee may, however, be consulted on systemic issues arising from patterns of complaints, subject to appropriate confidentiality safeguards.

Positive Action and Inclusion Initiatives

Consistent with Section 6.3, ISEA may adopt initiatives designed to broaden participation in the equity research profession and to support under-represented groups, where permitted by applicable law. Such initiatives may include:

scholarships, fee concessions or fee waivers to improve access to ISEA membership, examinations and certification for candidates from under-represented or lower-income backgrounds;

mentoring, sponsorship and leadership development programmes;

targeted outreach to universities, professional networks and communities that are under-represented within the profession;

diversity considerations in the composition of the Governing Council, committees and conference speaker panels, applied consistently with merit-based selection; and

chapter-level initiatives designed to reflect the cultural, linguistic and demographic context of the relevant jurisdiction.

Positive action initiatives shall be designed and implemented in a manner consistent with applicable law in the relevant jurisdiction, and shall not result in the appointment, admission or advancement of a less qualified individual over a more qualified individual on the basis of a Protected Characteristic.

Reporting Concerns and Complaints

ISEA encourages any person who experiences or witnesses conduct that they reasonably believe to be inconsistent with this Policy to raise the matter promptly.

16.1 Informal Resolution

Where appropriate and where the individual feels safe and comfortable doing so, concerns may first be raised informally with the person concerned, a committee chair, a manager, or another appropriate ISEA representative, with a view to reaching an early and constructive resolution. Informal resolution is not appropriate for serious allegations, such as sexual harassment or repeated misconduct, which should be reported formally.

16.2 Formal Complaints

Formal complaints concerning discrimination, harassment, bullying or victimisation shall be made in accordance with ISEA’s Complaints Policy. Complaints may be submitted to the Executive Secretariat, a designated EDI contact, or another channel identified in the Complaints Policy or Whistleblower Policy, and may be submitted by the person directly affected or by another person on their behalf, including anonymously where the Whistleblower Policy so permits.

16.3 What to Include

Where possible, a complaint should describe the conduct concerned, the individuals involved, the date(s) and location(s) of the conduct, and any supporting information or witnesses. ISEA recognises that individuals may not always be able to provide full details, particularly in the case of sensitive or traumatic incidents, and will not treat an incomplete report as a reason to decline to engage with a concern.

16.4 Support for Complainants

ISEA will treat all reports made under this Policy seriously, sensitively and with appropriate urgency, and will take reasonable steps to support the wellbeing of individuals involved in a complaint, including, where appropriate, by facilitating access to independent counselling or support services and by considering interim measures, such as adjusting reporting lines, meeting arrangements or event participation, pending resolution of the matter.

Protection Against Retaliation

ISEA prohibits retaliation against any person who, in good faith, reports a concern, makes a complaint, provides information, or participates in an investigation under this Policy. Retaliation is treated as victimisation under Section 10 and as a serious form of misconduct in its own right.

Protections against retaliation under this Policy operate alongside, and are reinforced by, the protections available under ISEA’s Whistleblower Policy, which establishes additional protected reporting channels and safeguards for individuals who report suspected wrongdoing.

Investigation and Resolution

Formal complaints raised under this Policy will be investigated in accordance with ISEA’s Complaints Policy and, where the matter proceeds to a disciplinary process, the Disciplinary Policy.

ISEA’s investigation process is designed to provide:

a prompt and proportionate response, having regard to the nature and seriousness of the allegation;

an impartial investigation conducted by a person or persons free from material conflicts of interest;

appropriate confidentiality, in accordance with Section 22;

an opportunity for the person against whom an allegation is made to respond before any adverse finding is made against them; and

a documented outcome, communicated to the relevant parties to the extent appropriate and consistent with applicable confidentiality and privacy requirements.

Where an investigation identifies a breach of this Policy, ISEA may take remedial action, disciplinary action in accordance with Section 19, or both, as appropriate to the circumstances.

Disciplinary Consequences

Conduct found to breach this Policy will be addressed in accordance with ISEA’s Disciplinary Policy. Depending on the nature and severity of the conduct, and the role of the person concerned, possible outcomes may include:

mandatory EDI training or coaching;

a formal warning or reprimand;

removal from a committee, examiner, volunteer or representative role;

suspension or termination of membership, in accordance with the Membership Regulations;

suspension or withdrawal of an ISEA certification or designation;

exclusion from ISEA events, examinations or digital platforms for a defined or indefinite period;

for employees and contractors, disciplinary action up to and including termination of employment or engagement, in accordance with applicable local law and ISEA’s employment policies; and

referral to a relevant regulatory, professional or law enforcement body, where appropriate.

Disciplinary outcomes will be proportionate to the nature, seriousness and context of the conduct, any pattern of prior conduct, and the position of trust or authority held by the person concerned.

Training and Awareness

ISEA will promote awareness and understanding of this Policy through appropriate training and communication, including:

EDI training for Governing Council members, committee members and Executive Secretariat staff, to be completed upon appointment and refreshed periodically;

guidance and induction materials for examiners, assessors and volunteers acting on behalf of ISEA;

awareness materials for Members, made available through ISEA’s website, membership communications and continuing professional development channels; and

targeted training for individuals in roles carrying particular responsibility for receiving or investigating complaints under this Policy.

Persons who fail, without reasonable excuse, to complete training required of their role may be subject to appropriate action in accordance with the relevant governance, employment or membership requirements applicable to that role.

Monitoring, Data Collection and Reporting

ISEA will monitor the implementation and effectiveness of this Policy, including through:

periodic, voluntary and anonymised diversity monitoring of membership, certification candidates, committee composition and Governing Council composition, where permitted by applicable law;

tracking of the number, nature and outcome of complaints raised under this Policy, reported to the EDI Committee in aggregated and anonymised form;

periodic review of membership, examination, employment and event data to identify any unexplained disparities that may warrant further inquiry; and

periodic reporting to the Governing Council on EDI progress, initiatives and outcomes.

Any diversity data collected under this Policy will be collected on a voluntary basis wherever practicable, will be processed in accordance with ISEA’s Privacy Policy and applicable data protection law, and will be used only for the purposes of monitoring, reporting and improving equality, diversity and inclusion outcomes, and not for the purpose of making individual admission, certification, employment or disciplinary decisions.

Where practicable and useful, ISEA may benchmark its EDI monitoring data and initiatives against comparable professional associations and recognised international frameworks, in order to identify good practice and areas for improvement. Aggregated, non-identifying EDI metrics may be referenced in ISEA’s annual or governance reporting, at the discretion of the Governing Council.

Confidentiality and Privacy

ISEA will handle information relating to concerns, complaints and investigations raised under this Policy with appropriate confidentiality, disclosing information only to those persons who reasonably need to know it in order to progress a report, conduct an investigation, ensure procedural fairness, or comply with a legal obligation.

Personal information collected in connection with this Policy will be processed in accordance with ISEA’s Privacy Policy and applicable data protection law. ISEA will seek to balance the confidentiality interests of all parties with the requirements of procedural fairness, the need to conduct an effective investigation, and any applicable legal or regulatory obligations.

Relationship with Other ISEA Policies

This Policy operates alongside, and should be interpreted consistently with, other ISEA policies, including:

the Ethics Policy and Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct, which establish ISEA’s broader ethical framework;

the Complaints Policy, which establishes the process for submitting and handling complaints;

the Disciplinary Policy, which establishes procedures for investigating and resolving alleged breaches of ISEA requirements;

the Whistleblower Policy, which establishes protected channels for reporting suspected wrongdoing and safeguards against retaliation;

the Privacy Policy, which governs the handling of personal information;

the Membership Policy, Membership Regulations and Member Admission Framework, which govern membership eligibility, admission and status; and

the Conflict of Interest Policy, which applies where a conflict of interest arises in connection with a matter addressed by this Policy.

Where a matter is addressed by a specific procedure established by one of these policies, that procedure shall apply, together with the substantive standards established by this Policy.

Third-Party Contractors, Suppliers and Event Partners

ISEA expects contractors, suppliers, venues, sponsors, exhibitors and other third parties engaged in connection with ISEA activities to conduct themselves consistently with the principles of this Policy while engaged in that connection.

Where reasonably practicable, ISEA will:

include appropriate EDI expectations in contracts and event agreements with venues, suppliers, sponsors and exhibitors;

select event venues and suppliers with appropriate regard to accessibility, as described in Section 11.2;

make clear to third parties that conduct inconsistent with this Policy, including harassment of Members, staff or volunteers, may result in termination of the relevant arrangement; and

provide a channel, consistent with Section 16, through which Members, staff or volunteers may report concerns about the conduct of a third party encountered in connection with ISEA activities.

This Policy does not itself govern the internal employment or diversity practices of independent third-party organisations, but ISEA will take reasonable and proportionate steps, within the scope of its contractual relationships, to promote consistency with the principles of this Policy.

Illustrative Examples

The following examples are provided to assist understanding of this Policy. They are illustrative only, are not exhaustive, and do not predetermine the outcome of any particular case, which will depend on its specific facts and circumstances.

25.1 Membership Admission

An Applicant is refused Associate Membership on the stated basis that ISEA “prefers candidates from more traditional financial backgrounds.” If the Applicant otherwise meets the published admission criteria, this would raise a concern of discrimination on the basis of socio-economic or educational background and should be reported in accordance with Section 16.

25.2 Examination Accommodation

A candidate with a documented visual impairment requests an accessible examination format and additional time. Provided the request is properly evidenced, ISEA would generally be expected to provide Reasonable Accommodation under Section 11.3, absent a specific and substantial concern regarding the integrity of the assessment, which should itself be explained to the candidate.

25.3 Conduct at a Conference

At an ISEA-sanctioned conference, a senior Fellow repeatedly makes demeaning jokes about a junior analyst’s nationality in front of other attendees. This conduct is capable of constituting harassment under Section 8, regardless of whether the senior Fellow considered the comments to be humorous, and may be reported under Section 16.

25.4 Retaliation After a Complaint

A committee member who raised a good-faith concern about a colleague’s conduct is subsequently excluded from committee communications and denied a speaking opportunity previously offered to them. This may constitute victimisation under Section 10 and should be reported promptly.

Review and Continuous Improvement

ISEA shall periodically review this Policy to ensure that it remains appropriate, effective and consistent with developments in:

international human rights and equality standards and good practice;

applicable law in the jurisdictions in which ISEA, its chapters and its Members operate;

the composition, needs and expectations of ISEA’s global membership; and

the evolving needs of the equity research profession.

The EDI Committee shall recommend amendments to this Policy where appropriate, having regard to monitoring data collected under Section 21, complaint trends, and feedback from Members and stakeholders, subject to approval by the Governing Council.

Effective Date

This Equality, Diversity and Inclusion Policy takes effect on the date approved by the Governing Council.

Governance Document
Governance Policy

Ethics Policy

International Society of Equity Analysts

DOCUMENT VERSION 1.0 DATE APPROVED 1 July 2026
LAST UPDATED 1 July 2026 ADMINISTERED BY Ethics and Professional Standards Committee
This document forms part of the official governance framework of the International Society of Equity Analysts (ISEA) and should be read together with the related documents listed above.

Purpose

The International Society of Equity Analysts (ISEA) is committed to maintaining high standards of integrity, professionalism, independence, competence and ethical conduct within the global equity research and analysis profession.

This Ethics Policy establishes the ethical framework governing ISEA's Members, holders of ISEA professional certifications and designations, Governing Council members, officers, committee members, volunteers and representatives acting on behalf of ISEA.

ISEA recognises that confidence in equity research and investment analysis depends upon the professionalism, objectivity, competence and ethical conduct of those engaged in the profession.

Accordingly, ISEA has established a Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct (“Code”) as the principal ethical and professional framework applicable to ISEA Members and other persons to whom the Code applies.

The Code reflects ISEA's commitment to promoting high standards of professional conduct, strengthening confidence in equity research and supporting the integrity, credibility and development of the global equity analysis profession.

This Ethics Policy operates alongside the Code and other applicable ISEA policies, regulations and governance requirements.

Scope and Application

This Ethics Policy applies to:

the Governing Council members;

officers of ISEA;

committee members;

ISEA Members (Student Members, Associate Members, Members and Fellows);

holders of ISEA professional certifications and designations;

volunteers and representatives acting on behalf of ISEA; and

individuals participating in ISEA-recognised professional activities, where applicable.

The Code applies to the persons and activities specified within that Code.

By becoming a Member of ISEA, obtaining an ISEA certification or designation, holding an ISEA governance or representative position, or participating in an ISEA professional program or activity, an individual acknowledges the ethical obligations applicable to their role.

Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct

ISEA has established the Code as the principal ethical framework governing the professional conduct of its Members and other persons to whom the Code applies.

The Code establishes principles and standards relating to matters including:

professional integrity and responsibility;

research independence and objectivity;

conflicts of interest;

fair dealing and professional relationships;

confidentiality and material non-public information;

research quality and disclosure;

plagiarism and intellectual integrity;

technology, automation and artificial intelligence;

professional competence and continuing development;

responsibilities to ISEA and the profession; and

professional misconduct and cooperation with ISEA processes.

Members and other persons subject to the Code are responsible for understanding and complying with the requirements applicable to them.

The Code may be amended from time to time in accordance with ISEA's governance and approval procedures.

Relationship Between this Policy and Other ISEA Requirements

This Ethics Policy establishes ISEA's overarching commitment to ethical and professional conduct.

The Code establishes the specific ethical principles and professional standards applicable to Members and other persons within its scope.

This Policy should be read together with other ISEA policies and procedures relevant to ethical conduct, including:

the Conflict of Interest Policy, which establishes requirements for identifying, disclosing and managing conflicts of interest;

the Complaints Policy, which establishes the process for submitting and handling complaints concerning ISEA or persons subject to its requirements;

the Disciplinary Policy, which establishes procedures for the investigation, determination and resolution of alleged breaches of ISEA requirements; and

the Whistleblower Policy, which establishes protected channels for reporting suspected wrongdoing and safeguards against retaliation.

These policies operate together and should be interpreted consistently. Where a matter is subject to a specific procedure established by one of these policies, that procedure shall apply in addition to the substantive ethical requirements established by the Code.

Fundamental Ethical Principles

ISEA expects persons within its professional community to uphold the following fundamental principles.

5.1 Integrity

Members shall uphold high standards of professional integrity and act honestly and responsibly in their professional activities.

Members shall avoid conduct that is inconsistent with the ethical standards of ISEA or that could materially undermine confidence in the equity research profession.

5.2 Independence and Objectivity

Members shall maintain independence of judgement and take reasonable steps to identify and manage circumstances that could compromise the objectivity of their research, analysis or recommendations.

Investment conclusions should be based upon appropriate evidence, analysis and professional judgement rather than improper commercial, personal or external influence.

5.3 Professional Competence

Members shall maintain and continually develop the knowledge, skills and analytical capabilities necessary to perform their professional responsibilities competently and effectively.

Members should remain reasonably informed of material developments affecting equity research, financial markets, analytical methodologies, technology and applicable professional requirements.

5.4 Transparency and Disclosure

Members shall provide clear, fair and appropriately prominent disclosure of material matters relevant to their research, analysis and recommendations, including applicable conflicts of interest, material relationships, significant assumptions, limitations and other matters that could reasonably affect an investment conclusion.

5.5 Responsible Use of Technology and Artificial Intelligence

Members who use artificial intelligence, automated systems, data analytics, programming tools or other technologies in professional activities remain personally responsible for the professional judgement, integrity and accuracy reflected in their work.

Members shall exercise appropriate oversight and verification and shall use technology consistently with their ethical, professional, confidentiality and other applicable obligations.

Responsibilities of ISEA Members

Members shall:

understand and comply with the Code;

comply with other applicable ISEA policies, regulations and professional requirements;

maintain appropriate professional competence;

conduct themselves consistently with the ethical and professional standards of ISEA;

protect confidential information obtained through their professional activities;

cooperate reasonably with legitimate ISEA inquiries, investigations and disciplinary processes;

report credible evidence of professional misconduct through an appropriate channel where required by the Code; and

avoid conduct that materially undermines the integrity or reputation of ISEA or its professional designations.

The specific obligations of Members are set out in the Code and other applicable ISEA requirements.

Responsibilities of Governing Council Members, Officers and Committee Members

Persons holding leadership, governance or committee positions within ISEA have additional responsibilities arising from their roles.

They shall:

act in the best interests of ISEA;

exercise independent judgement;

identify and appropriately manage conflicts of interest;

maintain the confidentiality of information obtained through their ISEA responsibilities;

protect the integrity and reputation of ISEA;

comply with applicable governance and fiduciary obligations;

exercise appropriate care in the performance of their responsibilities; and

lead by example in maintaining high standards of ethical and professional conduct.

The Governing Council, officers and committee members shall comply with applicable ISEA governance policies, conflict-of-interest requirements and other obligations applicable to their roles.

Conflicts of Interest

ISEA recognises that conflicts of interest may arise in professional, governance, assessment and other activities.

Persons subject to ISEA's conflict-of-interest requirements shall:

identify actual, potential and relevant perceived conflicts;

disclose material conflicts appropriately;

take reasonable steps to manage, mitigate or eliminate conflicts where appropriate; and

avoid allowing personal, financial, commercial or other interests to improperly influence professional or organisational judgement.

ISEA may establish additional conflict-of-interest procedures applicable to:

Governing Council members;

officers;

committee members;

certification assessors;

examination personnel;

education providers;

research contributors; and

other persons performing functions on behalf of ISEA.

Professional Misconduct

Professional misconduct is addressed principally through Standard 18 — Professional Misconduct of the Code.

Conduct that may constitute professional misconduct includes, but is not limited to:

dishonesty;

fraud or deception;

plagiarism or intellectual dishonesty;

falsification or fabrication of research or information;

material manipulation or distortion of analysis;

misuse of confidential or material non-public information;

serious or undisclosed conflicts of interest;

corruption, bribery or improper inducements;

market manipulation or other unlawful market conduct;

misuse or misrepresentation of ISEA membership or professional designations;

obstruction or improper interference with legitimate ISEA processes; and

other conduct fundamentally inconsistent with the ethical and professional standards expected of an ISEA professional.

The specific scope of professional misconduct and applicable Member obligations are governed by the ISEA Code.

Ethics & Professional Standards Committee

The Ethics & Professional Standards Committee is responsible for overseeing the development, interpretation and implementation of ISEA's ethical and professional standards, subject to the authority of the Governing Council.

The Committee may:

promote awareness of ISEA's ethical and professional requirements;

develop ethical guidance and educational materials;

recommend amendments to the Code and related policies;

provide guidance on ethical matters;

review or oversee alleged breaches in accordance with applicable procedures;

recommend appropriate disciplinary outcomes;

monitor emerging ethical issues affecting the equity research profession; and

promote continuous improvement of ISEA's ethical framework.

The Committee shall maintain appropriate confidentiality and procedural fairness in the performance of its responsibilities.

Enforcement and Disciplinary Actions

Where an individual is alleged to have breached the Code, this Ethics Policy or another applicable ISEA requirement, ISEA may undertake an appropriate review, investigation or disciplinary process.

ISEA's disciplinary procedures shall be designed to provide:

procedural fairness;

an appropriate opportunity for the individual to respond;

consideration of relevant evidence;

impartial consideration of the matter where practicable; and

proportionate outcomes having regard to the nature and circumstances of the conduct.

Subject to applicable ISEA disciplinary procedures, possible outcomes may include:

education or remediation;

formal warning;

reprimand;

suspension of membership;

suspension or withdrawal of an ISEA certification or designation;

restrictions on participation in ISEA activities;

termination of membership; or

referral to a relevant regulatory, professional or other appropriate body.

Confidentiality and Privacy

ISEA shall handle information concerning ethical matters, complaints, investigations and disciplinary proceedings with appropriate confidentiality and in accordance with applicable privacy and other legal requirements.

Information may be disclosed where:

required by law;

authorised under applicable ISEA procedures;

necessary for the proper conduct of an investigation or disciplinary process;

necessary to protect the integrity of ISEA or its professional standards;

required for legitimate regulatory or professional cooperation; or

otherwise authorised by the Governing Council or an authorised ISEA body.

ISEA shall seek to balance appropriate confidentiality with the requirements of procedural fairness, regulatory cooperation and the proper administration of its professional standards.

Review and Continuous Improvement

ISEA shall periodically review this Ethics Policy and its broader ethical framework to ensure that they remain appropriate having regard to:

developments in equity research and investment analysis;

international professional practices;

regulatory and legal developments;

technological and artificial intelligence developments;

emerging ethical issues; and

the evolving needs of the equity research profession.

The Ethics & Professional Standards Committee shall recommend amendments where appropriate, subject to approval by the Governing Council.

ISEA may also amend its Code through the governance process established for that Code.

Effective Date

This Ethics Policy takes effect on the date approved by the Governing Council.

Governance Document
Governance Policy

Financial Management and Internal Controls Policy

International Society of Equity Analysts

DOCUMENT VERSION 1.2 DATE APPROVED 1 July 2025
LAST UPDATED 1 July 2026 ADMINISTERED BY Audit, Risk and Compliance Committee
This document forms part of the official governance framework of the International Society of Equity Analysts (ISEA) and should be read together with the related documents listed above.

Purpose

The International Society of Equity Analysts (ISEA) is committed to maintaining sound financial management, effective internal controls, financial accountability and responsible stewardship of its financial resources.

This Financial Management and Internal Controls Policy (“Policy”) establishes the principles, controls and responsibilities governing the management of ISEA’s financial affairs.

The purpose of this Policy is to ensure that ISEA:

manages its financial resources prudently and in accordance with its objectives;

maintains accurate, complete and timely financial records and reports;

protects ISEA funds and assets from loss, misuse, fraud, error and unauthorised expenditure;

maintains appropriate controls over budgeting, purchasing, expenditure, banking and payments;

ensures that financial decisions are made within approved delegations and authority;

maintains appropriate segregation of financial duties;

identifies and appropriately manages financial conflicts and related-party transactions;

maintains appropriate financial reserves and liquidity;

provides the Governing Council with sufficient financial information to discharge its oversight responsibilities; and

maintains appropriate audit, review and assurance arrangements.

This Policy forms part of ISEA’s broader governance, risk management and accountability framework and shall be interpreted consistently with the ISEA Charter and other applicable ISEA policies, regulations and governance requirements.

Scope and Application

This Policy applies to:

the Governing Council;

the Secretary-General and other officers of ISEA;

members of the Executive Secretariat;

committee members where they exercise financial authority or incur expenditure on behalf of ISEA;

employees and contractors involved in financial administration or expenditure;

volunteers or other persons authorised to handle ISEA funds or incur expenditure on behalf of ISEA; and

any other person exercising a financial delegation or authority on behalf of ISEA.

This Policy applies to all ISEA financial activities, accounts, funds, assets, transactions and commitments, regardless of the jurisdiction in which they occur or the currency in which they are denominated.

Persons exercising financial authority on behalf of ISEA shall comply with this Policy, applicable financial delegations and any procedures established under it.

Where a person is uncertain about the application of this Policy, the matter shall be referred to the Secretary-General or other authorised officer for determination.

Financial Management Principles

ISEA shall manage its financial affairs in accordance with the following principles:

Accountability — persons entrusted with ISEA funds shall be accountable for the proper use and stewardship of those funds.

Prudence — financial decisions shall have regard to ISEA’s objectives, financial capacity, foreseeable obligations and longer-term sustainability.

Transparency — financial transactions and decisions shall be appropriately documented and capable of review.

Value for Money — expenditure shall seek to achieve appropriate value having regard to quality, suitability, cost, risk and the interests of ISEA.

Authorisation — expenditure and financial commitments shall be approved by persons with appropriate authority.

Segregation of Duties — key financial functions shall, where practicable, be separated so that no individual has inappropriate control over an entire financial transaction.

Integrity — ISEA’s financial resources shall not be used for personal, improper or unauthorised purposes.

Risk Management — financial risks shall be identified, assessed, managed and monitored consistently with ISEA’s Risk Management Policy.

Compliance — ISEA shall maintain appropriate compliance with applicable legal, regulatory, accounting, contractual and governance requirements.

Financial Governance and Responsibilities

4.1 Governing Council

The Governing Council has overall oversight responsibility for ISEA’s financial affairs.

The Governing Council shall:

approve ISEA’s annual budget and material revisions to the budget;

approve the financial framework and significant financial policies;

oversee ISEA’s financial sustainability and financial position;

monitor financial performance against approved budgets and strategic objectives;

oversee the maintenance of appropriate financial reserves;

approve financial delegations and material changes to those delegations;

oversee significant financial risks;

receive and consider periodic financial reports;

oversee the integrity of ISEA’s financial reporting;

oversee audit and financial review arrangements;

ensure that material financial irregularities, fraud or suspected misconduct are appropriately addressed; and

take such other financial oversight actions as are necessary to discharge its governance responsibilities.

The Governing Council may delegate specified financial authorities to the Secretary-General, committees, officers or other authorised persons, provided that such delegation is documented and remains subject to appropriate oversight.

4.2 Secretary-General

The Secretary-General is responsible for the day-to-day financial administration of ISEA within the authority delegated by the Governing Council.

The Secretary-General shall:

implement the approved budget;

ensure that appropriate financial controls are maintained;

oversee financial reporting and recordkeeping;

ensure that expenditure is appropriately authorised;

monitor financial performance and cash flow;

ensure that banking and payment arrangements are appropriately controlled;

ensure that financial risks and irregularities are escalated appropriately;

ensure that financial delegations are observed; and

report material financial matters to the Governing Council.

The Secretary-General shall not exercise a financial authority beyond the limits approved by the Governing Council.

4.3 Executive Secretariat and Financial Administration

The Executive Secretariat shall maintain appropriate financial administration systems and procedures, including:

accounting records;

budgets and forecasts;

invoices and supporting documentation;

payment records;

banking records;

reimbursement records;

asset records where applicable;

financial reports; and

other financial documentation required for proper governance and accountability.

Financial administration shall be conducted consistently with ISEA’s Document Retention Policy and applicable privacy and information-management requirements.

Budgeting and Financial Planning

ISEA shall operate on the basis of an approved annual budget.

The annual budget should be developed having regard to:

ISEA’s strategic objectives and approved activities;

expected membership and other income;

operating and program expenditure;

staffing and administrative costs;

contractual and other financial commitments;

expected capital or significant one-off expenditure;

financial reserves;

cash-flow requirements;

material financial risks; and

other matters relevant to ISEA’s financial sustainability.

The proposed annual budget shall be prepared by the Secretary-General or authorised financial administrator and submitted to the Governing Council for approval.

No person may knowingly commit ISEA to expenditure outside the approved budget unless the expenditure is:

within an approved financial delegation and otherwise authorised; or

subsequently approved through an appropriate budget variation or other authority established by ISEA.

Material variations from the approved budget shall be reported to the Governing Council.

The existence of an approved budget does not, by itself, constitute authority to incur expenditure. Individual expenditure must still satisfy applicable approval and delegation requirements.

Financial Reporting

ISEA shall maintain financial records that are sufficiently accurate, complete and timely to support effective management and governance.

Financial reporting shall provide the Governing Council with an appropriate view of ISEA’s:

financial position;

income and expenditure;

cash position and liquidity;

performance against budget;

material financial commitments;

reserves;

significant financial risks; and

other matters necessary for effective financial oversight.

Financial reports shall be prepared at intervals determined by the Governing Council or Secretary-General, having regard to the size, complexity and financial activities of ISEA.

Material variances between actual and budgeted financial performance shall be identified and, where appropriate, explained.

Financial reports provided to the Governing Council shall be sufficiently clear and complete to enable Council members to understand ISEA’s financial position and discharge their oversight responsibilities.

Expenditure Approval and Financial Delegations

ISEA shall maintain a documented system of financial delegations.

Financial delegations shall specify, as appropriate:

the person or role holding the delegation;

the type of expenditure or financial decision covered;

the applicable monetary limit;

any conditions or restrictions;

whether the delegation may be further delegated; and

any additional approval requirements.

A person shall not approve expenditure for which they do not have an appropriate delegation.

Financial delegations shall be exercised only for legitimate ISEA purposes and within the approved budget or other authorised financial framework.

A person shall not approve their own expenditure, reimbursement or personal financial benefit.

Where expenditure involves a conflict of interest or related-party transaction, the requirements of Section 14 of this Policy and the Conflict of Interest Policy shall also apply.

The Governing Council shall periodically review financial delegations to ensure that they remain appropriate for ISEA’s activities and governance structure.

Segregation of Duties

ISEA shall maintain appropriate segregation of financial duties to reduce the risk of error, fraud, misuse of funds and unauthorised transactions.

Where practicable, the following functions should be separated:

initiating or requesting expenditure;

approving expenditure;

processing or making payment;

recording transactions;

reconciling bank accounts; and

reviewing or overseeing financial activity.

No individual should ordinarily have sole control over the initiation, approval, payment and reconciliation of the same transaction.

Where ISEA’s size, staffing or operational circumstances make full segregation impracticable, compensating controls shall be established, which may include:

independent review;

additional approval;

periodic transaction testing;

Governing Council oversight; or

other appropriate supervisory controls.

Any material limitation on segregation of duties shall be documented and appropriately managed.

Banking and Management of Funds

ISEA shall maintain bank accounts only with financial institutions approved by the Governing Council or under an authority expressly delegated by it.

Bank accounts shall be established and operated in ISEA’s legal name or such other name as is properly authorised.

ISEA shall maintain appropriate controls over:

opening and closing bank accounts;

authorised account signatories;

online banking access;

payment instructions;

changes to banking details;

bank reconciliations; and

access credentials and authentication mechanisms.

Changes to bank account signatories or electronic banking authorities shall require appropriate approval and verification.

Bank reconciliations shall be performed regularly and independently reviewed where practicable.

ISEA funds shall not be held in personal bank accounts except in exceptional circumstances expressly authorised by the Secretary-General and subject to appropriate controls.

ISEA funds shall not be commingled with personal funds.

Payment Authorisations

Payments made on behalf of ISEA shall be supported by appropriate documentation establishing:

the nature and purpose of the expenditure;

the identity of the payee;

the amount payable;

the relevant budget or financial authority;

evidence that the goods or services were received, where applicable; and

the required approval.

Payment approvals shall be consistent with applicable financial delegations.

Where practicable, payment processing shall be separated from payment approval.

Changes to supplier or beneficiary bank details shall be subject to appropriate verification before payment is made.

ISEA shall maintain appropriate controls against fraudulent payment instructions, including payment fraud, impersonation, business email compromise and unauthorised changes to payment information.

Purchasing and Procurement

Purchasing on behalf of ISEA shall be conducted fairly, transparently, prudently and with appropriate regard to value for money.

Persons responsible for purchasing shall:

purchase only goods and services reasonably required for legitimate ISEA purposes;

consider price, quality, suitability, reliability, risk and other relevant factors;

use approved suppliers where applicable;

obtain appropriate quotations or other evidence of value for significant expenditure where practicable;

avoid unnecessary or unreasonable expenditure; and

maintain appropriate records of material purchasing decisions.

Purchasing arrangements shall not be structured or divided for the purpose of avoiding an applicable approval threshold or financial delegation.

Where competitive procurement is impracticable due to the nature, urgency or specialised nature of the requirement, the reason should be documented and the expenditure approved in accordance with applicable delegations.

Persons involved in purchasing shall disclose and appropriately manage any actual, potential or perceived conflict of interest.

Reimbursements and Expense Claims

ISEA may reimburse reasonable and properly incurred expenses arising from authorised ISEA activities.

A reimbursement claim should:

relate directly to legitimate ISEA business;

be reasonable in amount;

be supported by appropriate receipts or other evidence, where available;

identify the purpose and nature of the expense;

be submitted within the timeframe established by ISEA; and

be approved by an appropriately authorised person.

Individuals shall not approve their own reimbursement claims.

Where the claimant is the Secretary-General or another person whose expenditure would ordinarily be approved by that person, the claim shall be approved by an appropriately authorised alternative authority.

Personal, excessive or unauthorised expenses shall not be reimbursed.

ISEA may establish detailed expense and reimbursement procedures, including applicable limits and categories of reimbursable expenditure.

Fraud Prevention and Financial Misconduct

ISEA has zero tolerance for fraud, theft, financial deception, deliberate misappropriation or other intentional misuse of ISEA funds or assets.

Persons subject to this Policy shall not:

misappropriate or misuse ISEA funds or assets;

submit false, inflated or misleading expense claims;

create or approve fictitious transactions;

falsify financial records;

circumvent financial controls or approval requirements;

make unauthorised payments;

use ISEA funds for personal purposes; or

otherwise engage in dishonest or improper financial conduct.

ISEA shall maintain reasonable measures to prevent, detect and respond to financial misconduct.

Suspected fraud, financial irregularity or material misuse of ISEA funds shall be reported through an appropriate ISEA reporting mechanism, including the Whistleblower Policy where applicable.

ISEA may investigate suspected financial misconduct and may take disciplinary, recovery, contractual, legal or other appropriate action.

No person shall suffer retaliation for making a report in good faith in accordance with ISEA’s Whistleblower Policy.

Related-Party Transactions and Financial Conflicts

ISEA shall manage related-party transactions in a manner that protects the integrity of its financial decision-making and the interests of ISEA.

A related-party transaction includes a transaction or proposed transaction between ISEA and a person or entity where the relationship could reasonably give rise to an actual, potential or perceived conflict of interest or personal benefit.

Persons involved in a proposed related-party transaction shall:

disclose the relevant relationship or interest;

refrain from improperly influencing the decision;

not approve their own related-party transaction; and

comply with applicable requirements of the Conflict of Interest Policy.

ISEA shall assess whether a proposed related-party transaction is:

necessary or appropriate;

on reasonable and appropriate terms;

in the interests of ISEA;

appropriately authorised; and

appropriately documented.

The Governing Council may require enhanced approval, independent review or additional disclosure for material related-party transactions.

Financial Reserves

ISEA shall maintain appropriate financial reserves having regard to its financial position, operating commitments, strategic objectives and foreseeable risks.

The purpose of financial reserves is to support:

financial stability;

continuity of essential operations;

management of unexpected financial pressures;

unforeseen or exceptional expenditure;

protection against significant fluctuations in income; and

longer-term organisational sustainability.

The Governing Council shall periodically consider the appropriate level and purpose of ISEA’s financial reserves.

ISEA shall seek to maintain sufficient liquidity to meet its foreseeable financial obligations as they fall due.

The Governing Council may establish specific reserve targets, restrictions or designated reserves where appropriate.

Material use of reserves outside approved purposes shall require appropriate Governing Council approval.

Financial Oversight by the Governing Council

The Governing Council shall exercise ongoing oversight of ISEA’s financial performance and financial sustainability.

Financial oversight shall include consideration, as appropriate, of:

actual financial performance against budget;

cash flow and liquidity;

financial reserves;

material financial commitments;

significant expenditure;

material variances;

financial risks;

fraud or suspected financial irregularities;

related-party transactions;

audit or financial review findings;

compliance with financial delegations; and

other matters that could materially affect ISEA’s financial position or reputation.

The Governing Council may request additional financial information, explanations, reviews or assurance where it considers this necessary.

Material financial matters shall be escalated to the Governing Council without undue delay where they may materially affect ISEA’s financial position, operations, reputation or compliance obligations.

Audit and Financial Review Arrangements

ISEA shall maintain appropriate independent review or assurance arrangements having regard to its size, activities, financial complexity, risk profile and applicable requirements.

The Governing Council shall determine, or approve the arrangements for determining:

whether an external audit or independent financial review is required;

the scope and frequency of financial reviews;

the appointment of an appropriately qualified auditor or reviewer;

the manner in which findings are reported; and

the process for addressing material recommendations.

Where an external auditor or independent reviewer is appointed, ISEA shall provide reasonable access to relevant financial records and information necessary to conduct the engagement.

Audit and review findings shall be considered by the Governing Council or an appropriately authorised body.

Material control deficiencies, significant financial irregularities or other matters identified through audit or review shall be appropriately addressed and monitored to completion.

The independence of any external auditor or reviewer shall be appropriately considered when appointing or renewing the engagement.

Financial Records and Documentation

ISEA shall maintain financial records sufficient to demonstrate:

the source and application of ISEA funds;

the nature and purpose of material transactions;

approvals and financial authorities;

banking activity;

expenditure and reimbursements;

contractual and purchasing commitments;

financial reporting; and

other matters necessary to establish appropriate financial accountability.

Financial records shall be maintained securely and retained in accordance with ISEA’s Document Retention Policy and applicable legal requirements.

Access to financial records shall be limited to persons with a legitimate need for access or persons otherwise authorised to obtain them.

Exceptions and Breaches

Exceptions to this Policy shall be permitted only where they are reasonable, documented and authorised by an appropriate authority.

No exception may be used to circumvent a legal requirement, the ISEA Charter, an applicable ISEA Regulation or another mandatory governance requirement.

A material breach of this Policy shall be reported to the Secretary-General and, where appropriate, the Governing Council.

Financial misconduct or conduct that may constitute a breach of another ISEA requirement may also be addressed under the Ethics Policy, Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct, Disciplinary Policy, Whistleblower Policy, Conflict of Interest Policy or other applicable ISEA requirements.

Relationship with Other ISEA Policies and Requirements

This Policy operates alongside ISEA’s broader governance and risk framework.

It should be read together with, as applicable:

the Charter;

ISEA financial delegations and procedures;

the Risk Management Policy;

the Conflict of Interest Policy;

the Ethics Policy;

the Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct;

the Whistleblower Policy;

the Document Retention Policy;

the Complaints Policy;

the Disciplinary Policy; and

other applicable ISEA policies, regulations and Committee Charters.

Where a matter is governed by a specific ISEA requirement, that requirement shall apply in addition to this Policy.

Where there is an inconsistency between this Policy and a higher-ranking ISEA governing document, the higher-ranking document shall prevail.

Review and Continuous Improvement

ISEA shall periodically review this Financial Management and Internal Controls Policy to ensure that it remains appropriate and effective having regard to:

ISEA’s financial position and organisational development;

changes in the scale and complexity of ISEA’s operations;

audit and financial review findings;

identified financial control weaknesses;

fraud, financial misconduct or other financial incidents;

changes in applicable legal or regulatory requirements;

developments in financial management and internal control practices;

technological developments affecting financial systems and payment security;

changes to ISEA’s governance structure or financial delegations; and

emerging financial risks.

The Secretary-General shall recommend amendments where appropriate, subject to approval by the Governing Council.

The Governing Council may direct an earlier review where a material financial event, control failure, audit finding or significant organisational change indicates that the Policy should be reconsidered.

Effective Date

This Financial Management and Internal Controls Policy takes effect on the date approved by the Governing Council.

Governance Document
Governance Policy

Gifts, Benefits and Hospitality Policy

International Society of Equity Analysts

DOCUMENT VERSION 1.2 DATE APPROVED 1 July 2025
LAST UPDATED 1 July 2026 ADMINISTERED BY Executive Secretariat
This document forms part of the official governance framework of the International Society of Equity Analysts (ISEA) and should be read together with the related documents listed above.

Purpose

The International Society of Equity Analysts (ISEA) is committed to maintaining the highest standards of integrity, transparency and professionalism in its dealings with Members, sponsors, partners, research providers, service providers, conference participants and other stakeholders.

This Gifts, Benefits and Hospitality Policy ("Policy") establishes the framework governing the offering, giving, soliciting and acceptance of gifts, benefits and hospitality by persons connected with ISEA.

ISEA recognises that gifts, benefits and hospitality, where improperly offered, given, solicited or accepted, may compromise, or may be perceived to compromise, independence, objectivity and professional judgement, and may give rise to actual, potential or perceived conflicts of interest.

This Policy is intended to protect the integrity of ISEA's governance, professional standards, membership processes and reputation, and to support the ethical principles established under ISEA's Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct ("Code").

This Policy operates alongside the Code, the Conflict of Interest Policy and other applicable ISEA policies, regulations and governance requirements.

Scope and Application

This Policy applies to:

the Governing Council members;

the Secretary-General and officers of the Executive Secretariat;

committee members;

ISEA Members (Student Members, Associate Members, Members and Fellows);

holders of ISEA professional certifications and designations;

volunteers and representatives acting on behalf of ISEA; and

contractors, service providers and other persons engaged by ISEA, where applicable,

(each a "Relevant Person").

This Policy also applies to gifts, benefits and hospitality offered by, or received from, sponsors, partners, research providers, companies, conference exhibitors, membership applicants and other external stakeholders in connection with ISEA activities.

By becoming a Member of ISEA, obtaining an ISEA certification or designation, holding an ISEA governance or representative position, or participating in an ISEA professional program or activity, an individual acknowledges the obligations applicable to them under this Policy.

Definitions

For the purposes of this Policy:

"Gift" means any item, product or other thing of value given or received without something of reasonably comparable value being given in exchange, including physical items, vouchers, tickets, discounts or other items of value.

"Benefit" means any advantage, favour, service or preferential treatment provided to, or by, a person in connection with their role or association with ISEA.

"Hospitality" means the provision of meals, refreshments, entertainment, travel, accommodation or similar courtesies extended in a business or professional context.

"Nominal Value" means a value that is modest by ordinary business and cultural standards, and that is unlikely to influence, or be perceived to influence, professional judgement or decision-making, as further described in guidance issued by the Ethics and Professional Standards Committee from time to time.

"Public Official" means any officer, employee or representative of a government, regulatory authority, stock exchange, central bank, or other public or statutory body.

Guiding Principles

ISEA expects Relevant Persons to observe the following principles when offering, giving, soliciting or accepting gifts, benefits or hospitality.

4.1 Integrity and Professional Judgement

Gifts, benefits and hospitality shall never be offered, given, solicited or accepted in a manner that compromises, or could reasonably be perceived to compromise, independence, objectivity or professional judgement.

4.2 Proportionality and Reasonableness

Any gift, benefit or hospitality must be reasonable and proportionate in value and frequency, having regard to the nature of the relationship, the occasion and ordinary business and cultural practice.

4.3 Transparency and Disclosure

Relevant Persons shall be open and transparent about gifts, benefits and hospitality offered, given, solicited or received, and shall disclose these in accordance with Section 9 where required.

4.4 No Improper Influence

Gifts, benefits and hospitality shall never be offered, given, solicited or accepted with the intention, or reasonably perceived intention, of improperly influencing a decision, research outcome, investment recommendation, membership or certification determination, disciplinary process or procurement decision.

4.5 Cultural Sensitivity

ISEA operates across jurisdictions in which cultural practices concerning gift-giving and hospitality may vary. Relevant Persons shall exercise sound judgement, and where local custom might otherwise exceed the standards set out in this Policy, shall seek guidance from the Ethics and Professional Standards Committee.

Permitted Gifts, Benefits and Hospitality

Subject to the principles in Section 4 and the disclosure requirements in Section 9, the following are ordinarily permissible:

gifts of Nominal Value, including branded promotional items and customary seasonal greetings items;

\

reasonable working meals and refreshments provided in connection with legitimate ISEA business, meetings or conferences;

attendance at conferences, seminars, training programs or industry events that is reasonably connected to professional development or ISEA's activities;

reciprocal hospitality of a modest and proportionate nature extended in the ordinary course of professional relationships with sponsors, partners, research providers and other stakeholders; and

customary courtesies exchanged between professional counterparts that are consistent with the principles in Section 4.

Prohibited Gifts, Benefits and Hospitality

The following shall never be offered, given, solicited or accepted:

cash or cash equivalents, in accordance with Section 7;

gifts, benefits or hospitality that are lavish, excessive or disproportionate to the occasion or relationship;

gifts, benefits or hospitality offered, given, solicited or accepted with an expectation, express or implied, of influencing any decision, research outcome, investment recommendation, membership or certification determination, disciplinary process or procurement decision;

gifts, benefits or hospitality offered, given, solicited or accepted secretly, or otherwise than through open and transparent channels;

gifts, benefits or hospitality that would breach applicable anti-bribery, anti-corruption or other laws, including those concerning Public Officials; and

repeated or frequent gifts, benefits or hospitality from the same source which, whether individually or cumulatively, exceed the standards set out in this Policy.

Cash and Cash Equivalents
