Current Fee amounts are published in the Fee Schedule available on ISEA's official website, and prevail over any illustrative figures referenced elsewhere.

Fee Setting, Review and Publication

The Governing Council shall determine the amount of each Fee, having regard to ISEA's operating costs, market conditions, comparable professional bodies and the financial sustainability of ISEA.

Fees shall be reviewed by the Governing Council not less than once every financial year, and may be amended at any time where the Governing Council considers this necessary.

Current Fees shall be published on ISEA's official website and made available to applicants and members upon request.

Any amendment to a Fee shall not apply retrospectively to a Fee already paid, but shall apply to Fees becoming payable on or after the effective date of the amendment.

Where a Fee amendment is adopted, ISEA shall provide reasonable notice to members prior to the amended Fee taking effect wherever practicable.

Payment Methods and Currency

Fees may be paid by any Payment Method made available by ISEA from time to time, which may include:

credit card or debit card payment;

electronic funds transfer or bank transfer;

approved third-party online payment platforms;

direct debit or recurring payment authorisation; and

such other Payment Method as ISEA may approve.

All Fees are payable in the currency specified by ISEA at the time of invoicing, which will ordinarily be United States dollars unless otherwise stated.

Where a member elects to pay in a currency other than the currency specified by ISEA, any currency conversion, foreign transaction charge or bank fee arising from that election is the responsibility of the member.

ISEA is not responsible for exchange rate fluctuations between the date an invoice is issued and the date payment is received.

Payment Obligations and Due Dates

A member's obligation to pay applicable Fees continues regardless of whether the member actively participates in ISEA activities, uses membership benefits, or intends to apply for another membership class.

Application fees are due and payable at the time an application is submitted, unless ISEA specifies an alternative arrangement.

Renewal fees are due and payable by the renewal date determined in accordance with the Membership Regulations, whether that date is a common membership renewal date, an anniversary-based renewal date, or such other date as the Governing Council may establish.

ISEA may issue reminders in advance of a payment due date as a courtesy, but the absence of a reminder does not relieve a member of the obligation to pay applicable Fees by the due date.

Invoicing, Receipts and Tax Documentation

ISEA shall issue an invoice or payment request to a member or applicant prior to, or at the time of, a Fee becoming payable, specifying the amount, currency and due date.

Upon receipt of payment, ISEA shall issue a receipt or payment confirmation to the payer, which shall serve as evidence of payment for the member's records.

Where required by applicable law, ISEA shall issue tax invoices or equivalent documentation reflecting any goods and services tax, value-added tax or similar levy applicable to the Fee.

Members are responsible for retaining copies of invoices and receipts for their own taxation, reimbursement or record-keeping purposes.

Consequences of Non-Payment

Failure to pay an applicable Fee by the relevant due date may result in one or more of the following consequences, as determined by ISEA having regard to the circumstances:

issuance of a payment reminder or overdue notice;

imposition of a late payment charge in accordance with the published Fee Schedule;

suspension of membership rights, benefits and use of post-nominal designations;

removal from the Membership Register;

termination of membership in accordance with the Membership Regulations; and

referral of the outstanding amount for debt recovery, where ISEA considers this appropriate.

A member whose membership has been suspended or terminated for non-payment may apply for reinstatement in accordance with the Membership Regulations, which may require payment of outstanding Fees together with any applicable reinstatement charge.

ISEA may, in its discretion, grant a reasonable grace period or payment plan to a member experiencing genuine payment difficulty, having regard to the principles in Section 5 of this Policy and the fee waiver provisions in Section 17.

Failed, Declined and Dishonoured Payments

Where a payment is declined, dishonoured, reversed or otherwise fails to be received by ISEA in cleared funds, the underlying Fee shall be treated as unpaid until such time as payment is successfully received.

ISEA may charge a reasonable administrative fee to recover costs directly associated with a declined or dishonoured payment, including bank dishonour fees passed on by ISEA's financial institution.

Repeated failed payment attempts in respect of a recurring or automatic payment arrangement may result in ISEA suspending or cancelling that arrangement and requiring the member to arrange payment by an alternative Payment Method.

Nothing in this Section limits ISEA's rights under Section 13 in respect of non-payment.

Recurring and Automatic Payments

ISEA may offer members the option of authorising recurring or automatic payment of renewal Fees by direct debit, credit card or other approved Payment Method.

A member who authorises a recurring payment arrangement remains responsible for ensuring that valid payment details are maintained and that sufficient funds or credit are available on the applicable due date.

A member may cancel a recurring payment authorisation at any time by providing reasonable notice to ISEA, provided that cancellation does not relieve the member of any Fee obligation that has already accrued.

ISEA shall provide reasonable advance notice to a member before processing a recurring payment, where practicable, to allow the member an opportunity to review or cancel the arrangement.

Corporate, Group and Sponsored Memberships

Where an individual's membership Fees are paid or sponsored by a Sponsoring Organisation, the individual member remains personally responsible for compliance with this Policy and the Membership Regulations.

ISEA may, at its discretion, issue invoices directly to a Sponsoring Organisation, provided that appropriate authorisation and payment arrangements have been established with ISEA in advance.

Where a Sponsoring Organisation fails to pay a Fee on behalf of a member, the member remains liable for that Fee and is subject to the consequences described in Section 13 in the same manner as if the member had paid directly.

Refunds in respect of sponsored or corporately-paid Fees shall, unless ISEA determines otherwise, be made to the party that made the original payment.

Fee Waivers, Concessions and Financial Hardship

The Governing Council may establish, from time to time, categories of Fee concession, discount or waiver, which may include concessions for Student Members, early-career professionals, members in regions with lower relative income levels, or members experiencing genuine financial hardship.

A member seeking a Fee waiver or concession on the basis of financial hardship must submit a written request to ISEA, together with such supporting information as ISEA may reasonably require.

ISEA shall assess a hardship request having regard to the member's individual circumstances, the availability of concession funding, and the principles set out in Section 5 of this Policy.

A decision to grant or refuse a Fee waiver or concession is at ISEA's discretion and does not create a precedent binding ISEA in respect of any other member or any future application by the same member.

Information provided in support of a hardship request shall be treated confidentially in accordance with the ISEA Privacy Policy and Section 29 of this Policy.

General Principle of Non-Refundability

Membership Fees are generally non-refundable once processing of the relevant application, renewal, assessment or service has commenced.

This general principle reflects the fact that ISEA incurs administrative, assessment and operational costs upon commencement of processing, irrespective of the ultimate outcome of an application or the member's subsequent decisions.

The general principle of non-refundability in this Section is subject to the specific circumstances described in Section 19, in which ISEA may, in its discretion, consider a Refund.

Nothing in this Section obliges ISEA to grant a Refund in any circumstance; a Refund shall only be made where ISEA is satisfied, following assessment under Section 22, that a Refund is appropriate.

Circumstances in Which a Refund May Be Considered

ISEA may consider a Refund, in whole or in part, where one or more of the following circumstances is established to ISEA's reasonable satisfaction:

an Administrative Error occurred;

a Duplicate Payment was made;

exceptional circumstances exist;

a Required Service cannot be provided by ISEA; or

another basis approved by ISEA exists.

Administrative Error

Where ISEA identifies, or a member demonstrates, that a Fee was charged, calculated or processed incorrectly as a result of an Administrative Error, ISEA shall correct the error and, where an overpayment resulted, refund the excess amount.

A Refund arising from Administrative Error shall ordinarily be made in full in respect of the amount overcharged, without deduction of any administrative charge referred to in Section 23.

Duplicate Payment

Where a member establishes that the same Fee has been paid more than once, whether due to a processing error, a repeated payment submission, or any other cause, ISEA shall refund the duplicate amount.

A member who becomes aware of a Duplicate Payment should notify ISEA as soon as reasonably practicable to facilitate prompt investigation and Refund.

Exceptional Circumstances

ISEA may consider a Refund where exceptional circumstances exist that, in ISEA's reasonable opinion, make it unfair or unreasonable to retain the Fee. Exceptional circumstances may include, without limitation:

serious illness, injury or bereavement affecting the applicant or a member of their immediate family;

circumstances beyond the applicant's control that prevented participation in an assessment or service for which the Fee was paid;

natural disaster, civil unrest or other significant disruption affecting the applicant; or

such other circumstances as ISEA, in its discretion, considers exceptional.

An applicant relying on exceptional circumstances must provide ISEA with reasonable supporting evidence, which ISEA shall treat confidentially.

Inability to Provide a Required Service

Where ISEA is unable to provide a Required Service for which a Fee has been paid, including due to cancellation, discontinuation or unavailability of the relevant service, ISEA shall refund the Fee attributable to that service, or offer an alternative service or credit, at the member's election where reasonably practicable.

Other Basis Approved by ISEA

The Governing Council, or a person or body to whom the Governing Council has delegated authority under Section 22, may approve a Refund on any other basis not otherwise described in this Section, where it considers this appropriate having regard to the guiding principles in Section 5.

Circumstances in Which Refunds Will Not Be Granted

Except as provided in Section 19, a Refund will not ordinarily be granted in the following circumstances:

the applicant simply changes their mind after processing has commenced;

an application is refused, or an applicant does not meet eligibility or assessment requirements, where the assessment or eligibility determination has already been undertaken;

a member fails to use membership benefits, attend an event, or complete an assessment for which they were eligible and able to participate;

a member's employment, personal or professional circumstances change after payment, other than as described under exceptional circumstances in Section 19;

membership is suspended, terminated or not renewed as a result of disciplinary action or a breach of ISEA's governance requirements; or

the request for a Refund is made outside the timeframe specified in Section 21.

ISEA's decision that a circumstance falls within this Section rather than Section 19 is subject to the review and complaints mechanisms described in Sections 32 and 34.

Refund Application Process

A member or applicant seeking a Refund must submit a written request to ISEA, using the form or process specified by ISEA from time to time, within twelve (12) months of the date the relevant Fee was paid, unless ISEA agrees to extend this timeframe in exceptional circumstances.

A Refund request must include, at a minimum:

the requester's name and membership number, if applicable;

the date and amount of the Fee paid;

the ground on which a Refund is sought, by reference to Section 19; and

any supporting evidence relevant to that ground.

ISEA may request further information reasonably necessary to assess a Refund request, and may decline to proceed with the assessment until such information is provided.

ISEA shall acknowledge receipt of a Refund request within a reasonable time, and in any event within ten (10) Business Days.

Assessment, Decision-Making and Delegation of Authority

Refund requests shall be assessed by ISEA staff with delegated authority from the Membership and Chapters Committee, having regard to the circumstances described in Section 19, the evidence provided, and the principles in Section 5.

The Membership and Chapters Committee may establish internal delegations specifying the value of Refund that may be approved at each level of authority, with Refunds above a specified threshold requiring approval by the Membership and Chapters Committee or the Governing Council.

A decision on a Refund request shall be communicated to the requester in writing, including the outcome and, where the request is declined in whole or in part, the reasons for that decision.

ISEA shall endeavour to determine a Refund request within twenty (20) Business Days of receiving all information reasonably required to assess the request, recognising that more complex requests may require additional time.

A person who is dissatisfied with a decision on a Refund request may seek review of that decision in accordance with Section 32.

Refund Amounts, Deductions and Administrative Charges

Where a Refund is approved, the amount refunded shall be calculated by reference to the Fee actually paid, less any amount properly attributable to services already provided or costs already incurred by ISEA, unless the Refund arises from Administrative Error or Duplicate Payment under Section 19.

ISEA may deduct a reasonable administrative charge from an approved Refund to reflect the processing, banking and administrative costs associated with the Refund, except where the Refund arises from Administrative Error or Duplicate Payment.

Any third-party transaction fee, currency conversion fee or payment processor charge incurred in connection with the original payment is not refundable by ISEA, except where such a fee arose directly from an Administrative Error.

Where a Fee covered more than one service or entitlement, and only part of that Fee is the subject of an approved Refund, ISEA shall calculate a proportionate Refund by reference to the value of the unprovided portion.

Timeframes for Processing Refunds

Once a Refund has been approved, ISEA shall process payment of the Refund within twenty (20) Business Days, subject to the payment processing timeframes of the relevant financial institution or payment processor.

ISEA is not responsible for delays in a Refund reaching a member's account that are caused by the member's bank, card issuer or payment processor, and not by ISEA.

Where a Refund cannot be processed within the timeframe specified in this Section due to circumstances beyond ISEA's reasonable control, ISEA shall notify the requester of the delay and the expected revised timeframe.

Method and Currency of Refund Payments

A Refund shall ordinarily be made using the same Payment Method and to the same payment source used for the original payment, unless this is not reasonably practicable, in which case ISEA may arrange an alternative method in consultation with the requester.

A Refund shall ordinarily be made in the same currency in which the original Fee was paid.

ISEA is not responsible for any difference between the amount originally paid and the amount received as a Refund that arises solely from currency exchange rate fluctuation between the date of payment and the date of Refund.

Special Provisions for Assessment and Examination Fees

This Section applies specifically to fees paid in connection with the Equity Research Assessment, examinations, or other formal assessment processes administered by ISEA under the Member Admission Framework.

Where an applicant withdraws from a scheduled assessment more than thirty (30) days before the scheduled date, ISEA may, at its discretion, permit the applicant to transfer the assessment fee to a future assessment sitting rather than requiring a Refund request.

Where an applicant withdraws from a scheduled assessment less than thirty days before the scheduled date, the assessment fee is non-refundable except where the circumstances fall within Section 19.

Where ISEA cancels or reschedules a scheduled assessment for reasons within ISEA's control, affected applicants shall be offered, at their election, a transfer to the next available sitting at no additional charge, or a full Refund of the assessment fee.

A fee paid for re-marking, review of assessment results, or a supplementary oral defence is separate from the original assessment fee and is subject to its own refund treatment as specified by ISEA at the time such a service is offered.

Special Provisions for Fellowship and CPD-Related Fees

This Section applies specifically to fees paid in connection with Fellowship admission and Continuing Professional Development ("CPD") activities administered or endorsed by ISEA.

Fellowship application fees are subject to the general principle of non-refundability in Section 18, and may only be refunded in accordance with Section 19.

Where a member pays a fee for a CPD activity delivered directly by ISEA and that activity is cancelled by ISEA, the member shall be entitled to a full Refund or a credit toward a future CPD activity, at the member's election.

Where a member withdraws from a CPD activity delivered directly by ISEA, any Refund shall be assessed having regard to the notice provided and the costs already incurred by ISEA in organising the activity, applying the principles in Section 23.

This Policy does not govern fees charged by third-party CPD providers whose activities are merely recognised or accredited by ISEA; such fees are a matter between the member and the relevant third-party provider.

Taxes, Levies and Statutory Charges

Where a Fee included an amount for goods and services tax, value-added tax or a similar statutory levy, any Refund of that Fee shall include a corresponding refund of the applicable tax component, to the extent required by applicable law.

Members are responsible for any taxation consequences arising in their own jurisdiction from the payment or Refund of a Fee, and should seek independent taxation advice where required.

ISEA shall issue a credit note or equivalent documentation in respect of an approved Refund where required by applicable tax law.

Record-Keeping, Privacy and Confidentiality

ISEA shall maintain accurate records of all Fees invoiced, payments received, and Refunds processed, for such period as is required by applicable law and ISEA's record-keeping requirements.

Personal and financial information provided in connection with a payment or Refund request shall be collected, used, stored and disclosed in accordance with the ISEA Privacy Policy.

Access to payment and Refund records shall be limited to personnel and authorised third parties who require such access to perform their duties, subject to appropriate confidentiality obligations.

ISEA shall not disclose a member's payment or Refund information to a third party except as required by law, as necessary to process a payment or Refund, or with the member's consent.

Fraud Prevention and Payment Security

ISEA shall take reasonable steps to protect the security of payment information, including through the use of reputable, PCI-compliant payment processors and encryption of sensitive payment data.

ISEA does not store full credit card or payment card numbers on its own systems, other than through secure, tokenised arrangements with authorised payment processors.

ISEA may decline to process a payment, or may suspend a membership pending investigation, where it reasonably suspects that a payment is fraudulent, unauthorised, or made using stolen or compromised payment details.

A member who suspects that their payment information has been compromised should notify ISEA immediately so that appropriate protective steps can be taken.

Where a payment is later found to have been made fraudulently or without proper authorisation, ISEA may reverse any membership status, benefit or Refund obtained as a result of that payment.

Force Majeure

ISEA shall not be liable for any delay or failure to perform an obligation under this Policy, including the processing of a payment or Refund, to the extent that such delay or failure arises from circumstances beyond ISEA's reasonable control, including natural disaster, pandemic, war, civil unrest, industrial action, or failure of a third-party payment system.

Where a force majeure event affects ISEA's ability to process payments or Refunds, ISEA shall take reasonable steps to notify affected members and to resume normal processing as soon as reasonably practicable.

Disputes and Complaints

A person who disputes the amount of a Fee, the outcome of a Refund request, or any other matter arising under this Policy may raise that dispute with ISEA in writing, setting out the basis of the dispute.

ISEA shall review a dispute raised under this Section through a person who was not directly involved in the original decision, where reasonably practicable.

Where a dispute cannot be resolved informally, the person may lodge a formal complaint in accordance with the ISEA Complaints Policy.

Nothing in this Policy limits a member's rights under the Membership Regulations to seek review of a decision affecting their membership status.

Reporting and Financial Oversight

The Membership and Chapters Committee shall provide the Governing Council with periodic reports on Fee revenue, outstanding amounts, and Refunds granted, at intervals determined by the Governing Council.

ISEA's financial records relating to Fees and Refunds shall be subject to ISEA's ordinary financial control, audit and reporting processes.

Any pattern of Refund requests indicating a systemic issue with the administration of Fees shall be reported to the Governing Council with recommendations for remediation.

Notices and Communications

Any notice, invoice, reminder or communication given by ISEA under this Policy may be given electronically, including by email to the address recorded in the Membership Register, unless applicable law requires otherwise.

A member is responsible for ensuring that ISEA holds current and accurate contact details, and ISEA is not responsible for a member's failure to receive a communication sent to an outdated address.

A communication sent electronically in accordance with this Section is taken to have been received on the day it is sent, unless the sender receives notice that the communication was not delivered.

Severability

If any provision of this Policy is held to be invalid, unlawful or unenforceable in any respect under applicable law, that provision shall be severed from the remainder of this Policy, which shall continue in full force and effect.

Delegation, Amendment and Review of this Policy

The Governing Council may delegate any function under this Policy to the Membership and Chapters Committee, a sub-committee, or ISEA staff, subject to such conditions as the Governing Council considers appropriate.

This Policy may be amended by the Governing Council from time to time, including to reflect changes in ISEA's operating costs, applicable law, or the introduction of new membership services.

This Policy shall be reviewed by the Governing Council not less than once every three years, or earlier if the Governing Council considers a review necessary.

Amendments to this Policy shall be published and communicated to members in accordance with ISEA's ordinary governance communication practices.

Illustrative Examples

This Section sets out illustrative examples of how the refund provisions of this Policy may apply in practice. These examples are provided for guidance only, do not form part of the operative provisions of this Policy, and do not limit ISEA's discretion to assess each Refund request on its own facts.

Example 1 — Administrative Error

A member is charged the Fellow renewal Fee in error, when the correct Fee for their membership class was the Member renewal Fee. On review, ISEA identifies the Administrative Error and refunds the difference in full, without any administrative deduction, consistent with Section 19 and Section 23.

Example 2 — Duplicate Payment

An applicant's payment is submitted twice due to a browser error during checkout. ISEA identifies both payments during reconciliation and refunds the duplicate transaction in full to the original payment source.

Example 3 — Exceptional Circumstances

An applicant enrolled in the Equity Research Assessment is hospitalised the week of the scheduled oral defence and is unable to attend. The applicant provides medical evidence. ISEA offers the applicant a transfer to the next available sitting at no additional charge, in preference to a cash Refund, consistent with Section 26; where a transfer is not suitable to the applicant's circumstances, a Refund may be considered.

Example 4 — Required Service Cannot Be Provided

ISEA cancels a scheduled assessment sitting due to unavailability of assessors. Affected applicants are offered a full Refund of the assessment fee or a transfer to the next sitting at no additional charge, at their election, consistent with Section 26.

Example 5 — Change of Mind (Refund Not Granted)

An applicant submits a Member application, pays the application fee, and two days later decides not to proceed because they have accepted a role outside the investment profession. Processing of the application has already commenced. Consistent with Section 20, the application fee is not refunded, as this circumstance does not fall within Section 19.

Example 6 — Unsuccessful Application (Refund Not Granted)

An applicant completes the Equity Research Assessment but does not achieve the required standard. The assessment has been fully administered and marked. Consistent with Section 20, the assessment fee is not refunded, as an unsuccessful outcome following completed assessment is not, of itself, a ground for a Refund under Section 19.

Example 7 — Sponsored Membership

A member's renewal Fee is paid by their employer under a corporate sponsorship arrangement. The member resigns from their employer shortly after renewal and requests that the Fee be refunded to them personally. Consistent with Section 16, any approved Refund would be made to the Sponsoring Organisation that made the original payment, not to the individual member, unless the Sponsoring Organisation agrees otherwise in writing.

Interpretation

Headings in this Policy are for convenience only and do not affect interpretation.

A reference to a membership class, framework or other governance document is a reference to that class, framework or document as it exists from time to time.

Where any inconsistency exists between this Policy and another ISEA governance document, the order of precedence established in the Membership Regulations shall apply, subject to Section 4 of this Policy.

This Policy takes effect from the date approved by the Governing Council and remains in force until amended, replaced or revoked.

Governance Document
Governance Policy

Membership Policy

International Society of Equity Analysts

DOCUMENT VERSION 1.0 DATE APPROVED 1 July 2026
LAST UPDATED 1 July 2026 ADMINISTERED BY Membership and Chapters Committee
This document forms part of the official governance framework of the International Society of Equity Analysts (ISEA) and should be read together with the related documents listed above.

Purpose

The purpose of this Membership Policy is to establish the principles governing membership within the International Society of Equity Analysts ("ISEA").

This Policy provides the overarching framework for:

membership admission;
membership categories;
professional recognition;
member obligations;
membership progression;
maintenance of professional standards; and
the administration and governance of membership matters.

This Policy is intended to ensure that ISEA membership represents a meaningful professional affiliation based on competence, integrity, commitment to continuous development and adherence to professional standards.

Scope

This Policy applies to:

applicants seeking admission to ISEA;
existing ISEA Members (Student Members, Associate Members, Members and Fellows);
candidates seeking advancement between membership categories; and
committees, officers and personnel involved in membership administration.

This Policy operates together with the ISEA Membership Regulations and the Membership Framework.

The Membership Regulations establish the binding rules governing ISEA membership and shall apply except to the extent that this Policy expressly states an intention to override, amend or depart from a provision of the Membership Regulations.

An inconsistency between this Policy and the Membership Regulations shall not, by itself, constitute an override or amendment of the Membership Regulations. Where this Policy is intended to override, amend or depart from a provision of the Membership Regulations, the relevant provision of this Policy shall state that intention expressly and identify the provision of the Membership Regulations affected.

Membership Philosophy

ISEA recognises equity research as a specialised professional discipline requiring technical knowledge, analytical capability, independent judgement and ethical conduct.

ISEA membership is intended to recognise individuals who demonstrate professional competence and commitment to the advancement of equity analysis.

Membership is not intended to be merely a subscription, networking benefit or general association membership. ISEA membership represents professional recognition granted following satisfaction of defined admission requirements.

ISEA seeks to maintain membership standards that promote:

analytical excellence;
research integrity;
independent professional judgement;
ethical conduct;
lifelong professional development; and
contribution to the global equity research profession.

Membership Principles

4.1 Merit-Based Admission

ISEA membership shall be determined based on demonstrated professional competence, qualifications, experience, conduct and suitability.

4.2 Professional Integrity

Members must act honestly, independently and ethically in all professional activities associated with equity research and investment analysis.

4.3 Continuous Development

ISEA recognises that professional competence requires ongoing learning and development throughout a member's career.

4.4 Inclusive Professional Recognition

ISEA seeks to recognise professionals from diverse educational, geographic and career backgrounds while maintaining consistent professional standards.

4.5 Protection of Professional Designations

ISEA shall protect the integrity and reputation of its membership classes, post-nominals and professional designations.

Membership Categories

ISEA maintains membership categories designed to recognise different levels of professional development, experience, achievement and contribution to the equity research profession.

The membership categories of ISEA shall include:

Student Member — for individuals undertaking relevant education, training or early professional development activities relating to equity research, investment analysis or related disciplines;
Associate Member — for individuals who have commenced or are actively transitioning into professional practice in equity research, investment analysis or related disciplines, but who do not yet satisfy the experience, competency or assessment requirements for admission as a Member of the International Society of Equity Analysts (MISEA);
Member of the International Society of Equity Analysts ("MISEA") — for individuals who demonstrate the professional competence, experience and ethical standards required for recognition as an equity analyst professional; and
Fellow of the International Society of Equity Analysts ("FISEA") — for individuals who demonstrate exceptional professional achievement, experience, leadership or contribution to the equity research profession.

Each membership category represents a distinct level of engagement, recognition and professional standing within ISEA and shall be subject to separate eligibility requirements.

Admission to Student Member or Associate Member categories does not, by itself, confer entitlement to use any professional designation or post-nominal unless expressly authorised by ISEA.

The detailed requirements applicable to each membership category, including eligibility criteria, admission requirements, rights, benefits, progression pathways and renewal obligations, shall be prescribed in the Membership Regulations and the Membership Framework.

Admission Principles

ISEA shall assess applicants based on a combination of:

qualifications;
professional experience;
technical competency;
research capability;
ethical standing; and
professional judgement.

ISEA may require applicants to undertake assessments, submit evidence of professional capability, provide references, participate in interviews or complete other admission requirements determined appropriate by ISEA.

ISEA reserves the right to refuse admission where an applicant does not satisfy the required standards or where admission would adversely affect the reputation or integrity of ISEA.

Research Integrity and Professional Standards

ISEA recognises that the credibility of the equity research profession depends upon the independence and authenticity of professional analysis.

Applicants and Members must ensure that submitted research and professional work represents their own analysis, judgement and professional contribution.

ISEA does not prohibit the use of legitimate professional tools, including research databases, analytical software and technology solutions, provided that the Member remains responsible for the accuracy, independence and integrity of their work.

ISEA may take action where an applicant or Member engages in plagiarism, misrepresentation, fabrication, unethical conduct or other behaviour inconsistent with professional standards.

Member Obligations

Members are expected to:

comply with the ISEA Charter, Regulations, Policies, Framework and Procedures;
maintain professional integrity;
comply with applicable ethical standards adopted by ISEA;
maintain appropriate professional competence;
complete continuing professional development requirements where applicable; and
protect the reputation of ISEA.

Membership Renewal and Continuation

Membership is subject to ongoing compliance with ISEA requirements.

Membership renewal does not occur automatically and may be subject to:

payment of applicable fees;
compliance with professional obligations;
completion of required professional development; and
satisfaction of any continuing membership requirements.

ISEA may suspend, restrict or terminate membership where a Member fails to comply with applicable requirements.

Recognition and Advancement

ISEA recognises professional advancement through progression between membership categories.

Advancement is not automatic and requires evidence that the applicant satisfies the requirements applicable to the higher membership category.

The granting of a higher designation represents recognition of demonstrated professional achievement and contribution.

Administration of Membership

The Governing Council is responsible for the governance and oversight of membership matters.

The Governing Council may delegate membership administration, assessment and review functions to committees, officers or other authorised persons.

ISEA may establish procedures, guidelines and frameworks necessary for the effective administration of membership.

Fees and Membership Revenue

Membership fees are payable in accordance with requirements determined by ISEA.

Membership fees constitute general revenue of ISEA and shall be applied in accordance with ISEA's financial governance requirements.

Payment of membership fees does not create any entitlement to admission, renewal, designation or continued membership.

Review of Policy

This Policy shall be reviewed periodically to ensure continued alignment with:

professional standards;
industry expectations;
the strategic objectives of ISEA; and
the development of the equity research profession.

The Governing Council may amend this Policy from time to time.

Governance Document
Governance Policy

Publication and Editorial Policy

International Society of Equity Analysts

DOCUMENT VERSION 1.2 DATE APPROVED 1 July 2025
LAST UPDATED 1 July 2026 ADMINISTERED BY Research Standards Committee
This document forms part of the official governance framework of the International Society of Equity Analysts (ISEA) and should be read together with the related documents listed above.

Purpose

The International Society of Equity Analysts (ISEA) is committed to producing and disseminating high-quality, credible, independent and professionally rigorous publications that contribute to the development of equity research, investment analysis and the broader investment profession.

This Publications and Editorial Policy (“Policy”) establishes the principles, standards and governance requirements applicable to publications produced, commissioned, sponsored, edited, reviewed, distributed or otherwise issued by ISEA.

ISEA recognises that its publications may materially contribute to professional knowledge, influence investment and research practices, and shape the reputation of ISEA and the equity analysis profession. Accordingly, ISEA is committed to ensuring that its publications are developed with appropriate editorial independence, intellectual integrity, transparency, accuracy and professional judgement.

ISEA's publications may include, but are not limited to:

the International Journal of Equity Analysts, published quarterly as ISEA's principal scholarly and professional journal;

Global Market Outlook Reports, published monthly;

White Papers;

Occasional Research Papers;

research reports and analytical studies;

professional guidance and technical publications;

conference and event publications;

educational publications;

policy papers and consultation documents; and

other publications approved or issued by ISEA.

This Policy is intended to:

establish standards for editorial independence and integrity;

establish appropriate peer review and editorial review processes;

establish requirements for authors and contributors;

ensure appropriate disclosure of conflicts of interest and relevant relationships;

establish procedures for corrections, retractions and other post-publication actions;

protect publications against plagiarism, fabrication, falsification and other forms of intellectual misconduct;

establish appropriate requirements for the use of artificial intelligence and other technology in publication development;

distinguish editorial content from sponsored content and advertising;

establish safeguards against editorial conflicts;

regulate the appropriate use of ISEA's name, marks and institutional identity in connection with publications; and

maintain appropriate disclaimers concerning the nature, purpose and limitations of ISEA publications.

This Policy operates alongside the ISEA Charter, Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct, Ethics Policy, Conflict of Interest Policy, Complaints Policy, Disciplinary Policy, Whistleblower Policy and other applicable ISEA policies, regulations and governance requirements.

Scope and Application

This Policy applies to all ISEA publications and publication-related activities, regardless of format or medium, including print, electronic, digital, online and other forms of dissemination.

It applies to:

the Governing Council;

the Secretary-General and Executive Secretariat;

members of the Editorial Board and editorial teams;

editors, associate editors and guest editors;

peer reviewers and other reviewers;

authors, co-authors and contributors;

research providers and external researchers engaged by ISEA;

committee members and other persons contributing to publications on behalf of ISEA;

employees, consultants, contractors and volunteers involved in publication activities;

sponsors and commercial partners to the extent that they participate in or support publication activities; and

any other person involved in preparing, reviewing, approving, editing, publishing, sponsoring or distributing ISEA publications.

This Policy applies to original content, commissioned content, contributed content, adapted content, reproduced material and content generated or assisted by artificial intelligence or other technological tools.

Where a particular publication has additional editorial, academic, professional or methodological requirements, those requirements shall apply in addition to this Policy.

Publications Covered by this Policy

ISEA may publish different categories of material for different professional, research, educational and institutional purposes.

3.1 International Journal of Equity Analysts

The International Journal of Equity Analysts (“Journal”) is ISEA's principal scholarly and professional publication.

The Journal shall seek to promote rigorous research, professional knowledge, analytical development and informed discussion concerning equity research, investment analysis, financial markets, valuation and related disciplines.

The Journal shall ordinarily be published quarterly.

ISEA may establish separate editorial guidelines governing submission, peer review, publication standards, authorship and other Journal-specific matters, provided that such guidelines are consistent with this Policy.

3.2 Global Market Outlook Reports

Global Market Outlook Reports are ISEA's periodic market-oriented publications intended to provide professional analysis, commentary, observations and perspectives concerning relevant developments in global financial markets and the investment environment.

The Reports shall ordinarily be published monthly.

The Reports shall clearly distinguish analytical observations, factual information, forecasts, assumptions and opinions where appropriate.

3.3 White Papers

White Papers may be published occasionally to examine significant professional, technical, policy, methodological or industry issues relevant to equity research and investment analysis.

White Papers should ordinarily identify their purpose, methodology, sources and principal contributors.

3.4 Occasional Research Papers

ISEA may publish Occasional Research Papers addressing specific research questions, emerging issues, analytical methodologies or other matters relevant to the profession.

The level of review applicable to an Occasional Research Paper shall be determined having regard to its purpose, subject matter, intended audience and level of analytical or scholarly content.

3.5 Other Publications

ISEA may publish other materials, including professional guidance, technical notes, conference materials, educational resources, consultation papers and institutional reports.

The Secretary-General or designated editorial authority may establish appropriate review and approval requirements for such publications.

Editorial Independence

ISEA shall maintain editorial independence in the development, review, approval and publication of its editorial and research content.

Editorial decisions shall be based on appropriate professional, scholarly, analytical and editorial considerations and shall not be improperly influenced by:

sponsors;
advertisers;
commercial partners;
research providers;
Members;
companies or issuers;
financial institutions;
authors or contributors;
donors or other funding sources; or
other external or internal interests.

Editorial independence includes the authority to determine:

whether material is suitable for publication;
the editorial treatment of material;
whether material requires revision;
the selection of reviewers;
the acceptance or rejection of submissions;
corrections or other post-publication actions; and
the timing and manner of publication.

Financial or commercial support for a publication must not create an entitlement to editorial control or preferential treatment.

ISEA shall seek to maintain a clear separation between editorial decision-making and commercial, sponsorship and advertising functions.

Editorial Governance

ISEA may establish an Editorial Board, editorial committee or other appropriate editorial body to oversee publications.

The responsibilities of the relevant editorial authority may include:

establishing editorial standards;
approving publication processes;
overseeing editorial quality;
appointing or approving editors and reviewers;
overseeing peer review;
managing editorial conflicts;
reviewing significant complaints concerning publications;
recommending corrections or retractions;
monitoring publication integrity;
recommending improvements to publication processes; and
ensuring consistency with this Policy and other applicable ISEA requirements.

The editorial authority shall operate subject to the authority of the Governing Council and applicable ISEA governance documents.

Editorial decisions should, where practicable, be made independently of persons who have a material personal or commercial interest in the outcome.

Peer Review

Where a publication is intended to constitute scholarly or substantive research, ISEA should apply an appropriate peer review process.

The International Journal of Equity Analysts shall ordinarily be subject to peer review in accordance with the Journal's editorial requirements.

Peer review may involve:

assessment of methodological quality;
assessment of analytical reasoning;
assessment of the quality and adequacy of evidence;
assessment of originality or contribution;
review of citations and sources;
assessment of clarity and coherence;
identification of material limitations; and
other review appropriate to the nature of the submission.

ISEA may use single-blind, double-blind, open or other appropriate review models depending on the publication and circumstances.

Peer reviewers shall:

act objectively and professionally;
maintain confidentiality;
disclose relevant conflicts of interest;
avoid using unpublished material for personal advantage;
provide constructive and evidence-based comments; and
decline a review where they cannot provide an appropriately independent assessment.

Peer review does not guarantee publication and does not transfer responsibility for the integrity of the work from the author to the reviewer.

Author and Contributor Requirements

Authors and contributors are responsible for ensuring that submitted material is accurate, original, appropriately sourced and consistent with applicable professional and ethical standards.

Authors must:

ensure that submitted material is their original work or that they have appropriate authority to use the material;
accurately represent research methods, evidence, analysis and conclusions;
properly acknowledge sources and contributions;
disclose material conflicts of interest;
disclose relevant financial, professional, institutional or commercial relationships;
identify material limitations, assumptions and uncertainties where appropriate;
cooperate with reasonable editorial and review processes;
respond appropriately to requests for clarification or supporting information;
notify ISEA promptly where a material error is discovered after publication; and
comply with applicable ISEA policies and publication requirements.

Authors must not submit or publish material that is knowingly fabricated, falsified, plagiarised, materially misleading or otherwise professionally inappropriate.

Where multiple authors contribute to a publication, the authors should agree upon authorship and identify their respective contributions where appropriate.

Individuals who have made only minor editorial, administrative or technical contributions should not ordinarily be represented as authors solely on that basis.

Research Integrity and Accuracy

ISEA expects all research and analytical publications to be prepared with appropriate intellectual and professional integrity.

Authors and contributors must take reasonable steps to ensure that:

factual statements are supported by reliable sources;
data are accurately presented;
calculations and analytical methods are appropriately applied;
material assumptions are identified;
research methodologies are described accurately where relevant;
quotations and reproduced materials are appropriately attributed;
limitations are not deliberately concealed; and
conclusions are not materially misrepresented.

ISEA may request supporting data, research materials, methodological information or other evidence where reasonably necessary to assess the integrity of a publication.

Conflicts of Interest and Disclosure

Authors, editors, reviewers and other persons materially involved in publication decisions must disclose actual, potential and relevant perceived conflicts of interest.

Potential conflicts may include:

financial interests in a company or security discussed in a publication;
employment or consultancy relationships;
investment or commercial relationships;
sponsorship or funding relationships;
personal or professional relationships with authors or subjects of research;
relationships with companies, issuers or financial institutions discussed in a publication;
competing research or commercial interests; and
any other circumstance that could reasonably affect, or appear to affect, independent judgement.

Disclosures should be sufficiently clear to allow readers to understand the nature and significance of the relevant relationship.

Where a conflict cannot appropriately be managed, ISEA may require the person to:

recuse themselves;
withdraw from the editorial or review process;
appoint an alternative reviewer or editor;
include an appropriate disclosure; or
take another appropriate measure.

The existence of a disclosed conflict does not necessarily prevent publication. The relevant

consideration is whether the conflict can be appropriately managed while preserving editorial integrity and reader transparency.

Editorial Conflicts

Editors and editorial decision-makers must exercise independent professional judgement.

An editor must not participate in a decision where the editor has a material personal, professional, financial or commercial interest that could reasonably compromise or appear to compromise independence.

Editorial conflicts may arise where:

the editor is an author or co-author;
the editor has a close personal or professional relationship with an author;
the editor has a significant financial interest relevant to the publication;
the editor has a competing commercial or academic interest;
the editor has a material relationship with an organisation discussed in the publication; or
other circumstances exist that could reasonably call editorial independence into question.

Where an editorial conflict exists, the affected editor should disclose the conflict and, where appropriate, recuse themselves from the relevant decision.

ISEA may appoint an alternative editor or decision-maker where necessary.

Plagiarism and Intellectual Misconduct

ISEA does not tolerate plagiarism, fabrication, falsification, material misrepresentation or other forms of intellectual misconduct.

Plagiarism includes presenting another person's ideas, words, data, research, analysis, images or other intellectual work as one's own without appropriate attribution.

Plagiarism may include:

direct copying without appropriate attribution;
substantial paraphrasing without attribution;
presenting another person's research or ideas as original;
inappropriate reuse of previously published material;
undisclosed duplicate publication; and
other conduct that materially misrepresents authorship or originality.

Where plagiarism or other intellectual misconduct is suspected, ISEA may undertake an appropriate review or investigation.

Depending on the circumstances, ISEA may:

request clarification or supporting information;
require correction of the publication;
reject or withdraw a submission;
suspend publication;
issue a correction or retraction;
notify relevant institutions or professional bodies where appropriate;
restrict future publication opportunities; or
take disciplinary or other action under applicable ISEA requirements.

AI-Assisted Content

ISEA recognises that artificial intelligence, machine learning, automated research systems and other technologies may assist authors, researchers, editors and other contributors.

The use of artificial intelligence does not transfer responsibility for the accuracy, integrity, originality or professional judgement reflected in a publication.

Authors and contributors remain responsible for all material submitted to ISEA, including material generated or assisted by artificial intelligence.

AI systems must not be treated as independent authors.

Where artificial intelligence has been used in a material way in the preparation of a publication, ISEA may require disclosure of:

the AI system or tool used;
the purpose for which it was used;
the nature and extent of its contribution; and
any relevant verification or validation undertaken by the author.

AI-generated material must be appropriately reviewed and verified before publication.

Authors must take particular care to identify and correct:

fabricated information;
inaccurate citations;
unsupported claims;
misleading summaries;
invented sources;
biased or distorted outputs; and
other errors arising from the use of AI systems.

Confidential, personal, proprietary or otherwise protected information must not be entered into an AI system where doing so would breach applicable confidentiality, privacy, contractual or legal obligations.

ISEA may establish additional AI-use requirements as technology and professional practice develop.

Corrections and Amendments

ISEA is committed to correcting material errors in its publications in a timely and transparent manner.

A correction may be appropriate where a published work contains:

a factual error;
a material calculation error;
an inaccurate attribution;
an incomplete or inaccurate disclosure;
an editorial error that materially affects understanding; or
another error that should reasonably be corrected.

The form and prominence of a correction shall be proportionate to the nature and significance of the error.

Where practicable, the original publication should remain identifiable and the correction should clearly explain the nature of the amendment.

Minor typographical, formatting or editorial errors that do not materially affect meaning may be corrected without issuing a formal correction notice.

ISEA may also amend digital publications where necessary to correct non-material errors, provided that material changes are appropriately documented.

Retractions and Withdrawal

ISEA may retract or withdraw a publication where continued publication would materially undermine the integrity, accuracy or credibility of the publication or ISEA.

Grounds for retraction or withdrawal may include:

substantial plagiarism;

fabrication or falsification of data or research;

material research misconduct;

serious undisclosed conflicts of interest;

publication based on materially unreliable or fraudulent information;

significant legal or intellectual property concerns;

serious ethical violations;

material duplication or unauthorised republication; or

other circumstances that make continued reliance on the publication inappropriate.

A retraction decision should be based on a fair and appropriately documented review of the circumstances.

Where practicable, a retracted publication should remain identifiable as a retracted publication rather than being silently removed, unless legal, safety, privacy or other compelling considerations require removal.

A retraction notice should identify the publication concerned and provide an appropriate explanation for the retraction.

Sponsored Content

ISEA may publish or distribute sponsored content where doing so is consistent with its professional purpose and editorial standards.

Sponsored content must be clearly identified as sponsored, paid, commissioned or otherwise commercially supported.

Sponsorship must not give the sponsor editorial control over independent ISEA research or editorial content.

Sponsors must not be permitted to:

require a predetermined research conclusion;

suppress material findings;

require favourable treatment of a company, security or industry;

interfere with peer review;

select or remove independent reviewers solely to influence an outcome;

alter independent editorial conclusions; or

otherwise compromise editorial independence.

Where sponsored research or content is published, the nature of the sponsorship or funding relationship should be disclosed clearly and prominently.

Advertising

ISEA may accept advertising in publications or associated publication platforms where the advertising is consistent with ISEA's values, professional standards and reputation.

Advertising decisions should be separate from editorial decisions.

ISEA shall not accept advertising that:

is unlawful;

is materially misleading or deceptive;

is inconsistent with ISEA's professional standards;

creates a material conflict with the publication's purpose;

implies endorsement by ISEA without authorisation;

improperly uses ISEA's name, marks or professional standing; or

otherwise presents an unacceptable reputational or ethical risk.

Advertisements should be clearly distinguishable from editorial content.

Acceptance of advertising does not constitute endorsement by ISEA of the advertiser, its products, services, securities, investment strategies or claims.

Separation of Editorial and Commercial Functions

ISEA shall seek to maintain appropriate separation between:

editorial decision-making;

research and analytical activities;

sponsorship;

advertising;

commercial partnerships; and

other revenue-generating activities.

Persons responsible for commercial relationships should not improperly influence editorial decisions.

Similarly, editors and researchers should not use editorial authority to obtain personal or commercial benefits.

Where structural separation is not practicable because of ISEA's size or organisational arrangements, appropriate disclosure, recusal, review or other safeguards should be implemented.

Use of ISEA's Name, Logo and Institutional Identity

ISEA's name, logo, trademarks, professional designations and institutional identity may only be used in connection with publications in accordance with ISEA's authorisation and applicable branding requirements.

Authors, Members, sponsors, partners and other persons must not represent that a publication:

has been issued by ISEA;

has been endorsed by ISEA;

has been reviewed or approved by ISEA;

represents an official ISEA position; or

carries ISEA's institutional authority,

unless such representation is accurate and expressly authorised.

Use of the ISEA name in a publication does not, by itself, constitute endorsement of every statement, conclusion, recommendation or opinion contained in that publication.

Persons must not use ISEA's name, logo or institutional identity in a manner that could reasonably mislead readers concerning ISEA's involvement, endorsement or responsibility.

Disclaimers

ISEA publications should include an appropriate disclaimer having regard to the nature and purpose of the publication.

Where applicable, disclaimers should make clear that:

publications are provided for informational, educational, research or professional purposes;

publications do not constitute personalised investment, financial, legal, accounting or other professional advice;

opinions and forecasts are those of the relevant authors or contributors unless expressly stated otherwise;

forecasts and forward-looking statements are subject to uncertainty and may not materialise;

readers should undertake their own assessment and obtain appropriate professional advice where necessary;

publication does not constitute an offer, solicitation or recommendation to buy or sell a security unless expressly and appropriately authorised;

ISEA does not guarantee the completeness or accuracy of all information where appropriate; and

past performance is not necessarily indicative of future results, where relevant.

Disclaimers must not be used to excuse deliberate inaccuracies, misleading statements, research misconduct or failure to comply with applicable professional standards.

Complaints Concerning Publications

ISEA may receive complaints or concerns concerning the accuracy, integrity, authorship, editorial independence, conflicts of interest or other aspects of an ISEA publication.

Publication-related complaints shall be handled in accordance with the ISEA Complaints Policy where applicable.

Where a complaint raises potential plagiarism, research misconduct, undisclosed conflicts, professional misconduct or other serious concerns, ISEA may refer the matter to the appropriate governance, ethics or disciplinary process.

ISEA shall seek to ensure that publication-related complaints are considered fairly, appropriately and without improper interference with editorial independence.

Confidentiality

Editors, reviewers, authors, researchers and other persons involved in publication processes shall maintain appropriate confidentiality concerning unpublished manuscripts, research materials, peer review comments, editorial deliberations and other confidential information.

Confidential information must not be used for personal, commercial or other improper advantage.

Information may be disclosed where:

required by law;

necessary for the proper administration of the publication process;

necessary to investigate suspected misconduct;

authorised by the relevant editorial or governance authority; or

otherwise permitted under applicable ISEA requirements.

Records and Publication Integrity

ISEA shall maintain appropriate records concerning its publications and material editorial decisions.

Records may include:

submitted manuscripts;

review records;

editorial decisions;

author disclosures;

conflict-of-interest declarations;

sponsorship and funding disclosures;

correction and retraction records;

relevant correspondence; and

other records reasonably necessary to demonstrate the integrity of the publication process.

ISEA shall seek to maintain sufficient records to support accountability, transparency and the appropriate administration of its publication activities.

Responsibilities

23.1 Governing Council

The Governing Council is responsible for oversight of ISEA's publication framework and shall approve this Policy and material amendments.

The Governing Council may establish or designate an editorial authority responsible for implementing this Policy.

23.2 Secretary-General and Executive Secretariat

The Secretary-General and Executive Secretariat shall support the administration of ISEA's publication framework and may:

coordinate publication processes;

maintain publication records;

support editorial governance;

facilitate disclosures and conflict management;

coordinate publication of approved materials; and

escalate significant matters to the appropriate authority.

23.3 Editorial Board and Editors

The Editorial Board and editors are responsible for maintaining editorial standards and independence within their respective publications.

They shall exercise appropriate professional judgement and ensure that publication decisions are made consistently with this Policy.

23.4 Authors and Contributors

Authors and contributors are responsible for the accuracy, integrity, originality and appropriate disclosure of their work.

23.5 Peer Reviewers

Peer reviewers are responsible for providing independent, confidential and professionally appropriate assessments and for disclosing relevant conflicts.

Relationship with Other ISEA Requirements

This Policy should be read together with the ISEA Charter, Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct, Ethics Policy, Conflict of Interest Policy, Complaints Policy, Disciplinary Policy, Whistleblower Policy, Gifts, Benefits and Hospitality Policy and other applicable ISEA requirements.

The Code establishes the ethical and professional standards applicable to persons within its scope.

The Conflict of Interest Policy establishes requirements for identifying, disclosing and managing conflicts that may arise in connection with publication activities.

The Complaints Policy establishes procedures for receiving and handling complaints concerning ISEA and persons subject to ISEA requirements.

The Disciplinary Policy establishes procedures for addressing alleged breaches of ISEA requirements.

Where another ISEA document establishes a more specific requirement concerning a particular publication or activity, that requirement shall apply in addition to this Policy.

Where any inconsistency exists between this Policy and a higher-ranking ISEA governing document, the higher-ranking document shall prevail.

Review and Continuous Improvement

ISEA shall periodically review this Publications and Editorial Policy and its broader publication framework to ensure that they remain appropriate, effective and consistent with evolving professional standards.

The review shall have regard to:

developments in scholarly and professional publishing;

developments in equity research and investment analysis;

emerging standards concerning research integrity and publication ethics;

developments in artificial intelligence and other publication technologies;

changes in ISEA's publication portfolio;

experience arising from peer review, editorial processes, corrections and retractions;

emerging conflicts-of-interest risks;

regulatory and legal developments;

feedback from authors, reviewers, Members and other relevant stakeholders; and

international publishing and professional practices.

The relevant editorial authority or Committee may recommend amendments to this Policy, subject to approval by the Governing Council.

Effective Date

This Publications and Editorial Policy takes effect on the date approved by the Governing Council.

Governance Document
Governance Policy

Risk Management Policy

International Society of Equity Analysts

DOCUMENT VERSION 1.0 DATE APPROVED 1 July 2026
LAST UPDATED 1 July 2026 ADMINISTERED BY Audit, Risk and Compliance Committee
This document forms part of the official governance framework of the International Society of Equity Analysts (ISEA) and should be read together with the related documents listed above.

Purpose

The International Society of Equity Analysts (ISEA) is committed to identifying, assessing, managing and monitoring risks that could affect the achievement of its objectives, the integrity of its professional standards, the protection of its stakeholders and the sustainability and reputation of the Society.

This Risk Management Policy establishes the principles, responsibilities and processes through which ISEA identifies and manages material risks arising from its governance, operations, professional activities, financial affairs, technology, information management and external environment.

The purpose of this Policy is to:

promote a systematic and proportionate approach to risk management;

support informed decision-making by the Governing Council, committees and management;

protect ISEA's members, candidates, employees, volunteers, partners and other stakeholders;

safeguard ISEA's assets, information, professional standards and reputation;

support compliance with applicable legal, regulatory, contractual and governance obligations;

improve ISEA's resilience to operational disruption, emerging threats and unexpected events; and

encourage a culture in which material risks are identified and addressed rather than ignored or concealed.

Risk management is an integral part of ISEA's governance and decision-making and is not solely the responsibility of any individual committee or officer.

Scope and Application

This Policy applies to ISEA and to persons involved in the management or operation of ISEA, including:

Governing Council members;

officers and executives;

committee members;

employees and contractors;

volunteers;

representatives acting on behalf of ISEA; and

other persons with responsibility for ISEA activities where relevant.

This Policy applies to risks arising from or affecting:

governance and organisational decision-making;

membership and professional designation activities;

certification, examination, assessment and education programs;

continuing professional development;

equity research and professional standards activities;

events, conferences and professional programs;

financial management and commercial activities;

partnerships, sponsorships and external relationships;

technology, artificial intelligence and digital platforms;

information security, privacy and data management;

legal, regulatory and compliance obligations;

human resources and workplace matters;

business continuity and operational resilience;

communications and public reputation; and

other activities undertaken by or on behalf of ISEA.

This Policy applies to actual, potential and emerging risks and to risks arising from both internal and external sources.

Risk Management Principles

ISEA shall apply the following principles in managing risk:

3.1 Proportionate Risk Management

Risk management shall be proportionate to the nature, scale, complexity and potential consequences of the risk.

3.2 Accountability

Responsibility for managing a risk shall be assigned to an appropriate person or body with sufficient authority, competence and resources to manage it.

3.3 Integration

Risk considerations shall be incorporated into strategic planning, policy development, operational decisions, projects, investments and other significant activities.

3.4 Independence of Oversight

Where appropriate, risk identification, management and oversight shall be separated so that significant risks receive objective review.

3.5 Transparency and Escalation

Material risks shall be identified, documented and communicated to the appropriate level of authority. Individuals shall not knowingly conceal, minimise or misrepresent material risks.

3.6 Continuous Improvement

ISEA shall periodically review its risk-management practices and improve them in light of experience, emerging risks, incidents, technological developments and changes in the external environment.

Risk Appetite

ISEA shall maintain a risk appetite appropriate to its status as a global professional organisation.

ISEA shall seek to:

avoid unnecessary risks that could materially compromise its integrity, independence or professional standards;

accept proportionate and considered risks where doing so supports its strategic objectives and provides reasonable benefits to members or the profession;

maintain low tolerance for risks involving fraud, corruption, serious ethical misconduct, misuse of confidential information, material breaches of privacy obligations, significant conflicts of interest and conduct that could materially undermine the integrity of ISEA or its professional designations; and

maintain appropriate controls over financial, operational, technological and reputational risks.

The Governing Council may establish more detailed risk appetite statements or thresholds for specific areas of ISEA's operations.

Risk Categories

ISEA shall consider, where relevant, the following categories of risk.

5.1 Strategic Risk

Risks arising from decisions, developments or external circumstances that could prevent ISEA from achieving its strategic objectives.

Examples include:

ineffective strategic direction;

failure to maintain professional relevance;

inappropriate expansion;

changes in the equity research profession;

competitive pressures; and

failure to respond to emerging professional or technological developments.

5.2 Governance Risk

Risks arising from weaknesses in governance, oversight, decision-making or accountability.

Examples include:

inadequate oversight;

unclear authority or responsibility;

conflicts of interest;

ineffective committee structures;

poor recordkeeping; and

failure to follow approved governance requirements.

5.3 Professional and Ethical Risk

Risks arising from conduct that could undermine ISEA's professional standards or the integrity of the equity research profession.

Examples include:

ethical misconduct;

plagiarism;

research manipulation or fabrication;

conflicts of interest;

misuse of material non-public information;

inappropriate use of artificial intelligence;

misuse of ISEA designations; and

inadequate enforcement of professional standards.

5.4 Membership and Certification Risk

Risks associated with membership administration, certification, examinations, assessments and professional designations.

Examples include:

inaccurate membership records;

inappropriate admission or certification decisions;

examination integrity failures;

fraudulent applications;

misuse of professional designations;

inconsistent assessment processes; and

inadequate management of continuing professional development requirements.

5.5 Operational Risk

Risks arising from failures of processes, people, systems or external service providers.

Examples include:

operational errors;

inadequate procedures;

service interruptions;

key-person dependency;

supplier failures;

inadequate business continuity arrangements; and

failures in event or program administration.

5.6 Financial Risk

Risks that could adversely affect ISEA's financial position, liquidity, assets or sustainability.

Examples include:

inadequate liquidity;

inaccurate financial reporting;

fraud or financial misconduct;

poor financial controls;

excessive concentration of revenue;

investment losses;

unexpected liabilities; and

failure of significant counterparties or service providers.

5.7 Legal and Regulatory Risk

Risks arising from non-compliance with applicable laws, regulations, contractual obligations or professional requirements.

Examples include:

privacy breaches;

intellectual property infringement;

regulatory non-compliance;

contractual disputes;

employment-related obligations;

tax obligations; and

failure to obtain or maintain required permissions or registrations.

5.8 Technology and Cyber Risk

Risks arising from technology systems, digital platforms, artificial intelligence and cyber threats.

Examples include:

cyberattack;

unauthorised access;

data loss;

system failure;

inappropriate use of artificial intelligence;

technology dependency;

inadequate access controls; and

failures of third-party technology providers.

5.9 Information and Privacy Risk

Risks arising from inappropriate collection, use, disclosure, retention or protection of personal, confidential or proprietary information.

ISEA shall manage such risks consistently with its Privacy Policy, Information Security requirements, Document Retention Policy and other applicable policies.

5.10 Reputational Risk

Risks that could materially affect confidence in ISEA, its professional standards, its designations or the equity research profession.

Reputational risk may arise from:

member misconduct;

governance failures;

public controversies;

inadequate communication;

ethical breaches;

regulatory action;

poor service delivery; or

other events that could materially undermine stakeholder confidence.

5.11 People and Workplace Risk

Risks associated with employees, contractors, volunteers, committee members and other persons working for or on behalf of ISEA.

Examples include:

inadequate capability or resourcing;

misconduct;

harassment or discrimination;

workplace safety issues;

key-person dependency;

inadequate succession planning; and

loss of critical knowledge.

5.12 External and Emerging Risks

ISEA shall monitor emerging risks arising from developments including:

artificial intelligence;

changes in financial markets;

geopolitical developments;

economic conditions;

regulatory changes;

technological developments;

changes in professional practice; and

other external factors that could materially affect ISEA.

Risk Identification and Assessment

ISEA shall seek to identify material risks through:

strategic planning;

operational reviews;

committee and management reporting;

incident and issue reporting;

audits and assurance activities;

legal and regulatory reviews;

consultation with relevant stakeholders;

scenario and stress analysis where appropriate; and

monitoring of external developments.

Identified risks shall, where appropriate, be assessed having regard to:

the likelihood of occurrence;

the potential impact;

the speed with which the risk could materialise;

the effectiveness of existing controls; and

the resulting residual risk.

ISEA may use a formal risk-rating methodology approved by the Governing Council or an authorised committee.

Risk Register

ISEA shall maintain an appropriate risk register or equivalent mechanism for recording material risks.

The risk register should, where appropriate, identify:

the risk;

its source or cause;

potential consequences;

inherent risk level;

existing controls;

residual risk level;

risk owner;

planned mitigation measures;

target risk level;

review date; and

status of mitigation actions.

Material risks shall be reviewed at intervals appropriate to their nature and significance.

Risk Treatment and Mitigation

ISEA may respond to risks through one or more of the following approaches:

Avoidance — ceasing or not undertaking an activity where the risk is unacceptable;

Reduction — implementing controls to reduce the likelihood or impact of the risk;

Transfer — transferring an appropriate portion of the risk through insurance, contractual arrangements or other mechanisms;

Acceptance — accepting a risk where it falls within ISEA's risk appetite and is appropriately authorised; or

Monitoring — continuing to monitor the risk where further treatment is not presently required.

Risk treatments shall be proportionate to the level and nature of the risk.
