Where a risk exceeds ISEA's approved risk appetite, appropriate action shall be taken to reduce, transfer or otherwise address the risk unless acceptance is expressly authorised by the appropriate authority.

Risk Ownership

A material risk shall have an identified risk owner.

Risk owners are responsible for:

understanding the risks within their area of responsibility;

maintaining appropriate controls;

monitoring changes in risk exposure;

implementing agreed mitigation measures;

reporting material changes or incidents; and

escalating risks that exceed their authority or risk tolerance.

Delegation of operational responsibility does not remove the accountability of the relevant governing body, committee or executive responsible for the activity.

Control Environment

ISEA shall maintain controls reasonably designed to prevent, detect or mitigate material risks.

Controls may include:

policies and procedures;

segregation of duties;

approvals and authorisations;

access controls;

reconciliations;

contractual protections;

insurance;

training and awareness;

monitoring and quality assurance;

independent review; and

incident-response procedures.

Controls shall be reviewed periodically to determine whether they remain appropriate and effective.

Risk Reporting and Escalation

Material risks shall be reported to the appropriate level of management, committee or the Governing Council having regard to their significance.

Immediate or expedited escalation shall occur where a matter may:

materially threaten ISEA's financial position or viability;

materially compromise personal, confidential or material non-public information;

materially affect certification or examination integrity;

involve fraud, corruption or serious misconduct;

result in significant legal or regulatory exposure;

materially disrupt critical operations; or

materially damage ISEA's reputation or professional standing.

Reports to the Governing Council should, where appropriate, identify the nature of the risk, potential consequences, existing controls, mitigation measures and recommended actions.

Incident Management

ISEA shall maintain processes for identifying, recording, assessing, containing and responding to material incidents.

Where a material incident occurs, ISEA shall, as appropriate:

take immediate steps to contain the incident;

protect affected persons, information and assets;

assess actual and potential consequences;

notify appropriate internal authorities;

comply with applicable legal or regulatory notification requirements;

document the incident and actions taken;

conduct a post-incident review where appropriate; and

implement corrective or preventative measures.

Incident management shall operate consistently with applicable ISEA policies, including the Privacy Policy, Information Security Policy, Complaints Policy, Disciplinary Policy and Whistleblower Policy where relevant.

Business Continuity and Resilience

ISEA shall maintain proportionate arrangements to support continuity of critical activities following significant disruption.

Business continuity planning should consider:

critical operations and services;

key personnel and succession arrangements;

technology and system dependencies;

critical suppliers and service providers;

communications;

data and records;

alternative operating arrangements; and

recovery priorities.

ISEA may periodically test or review its business continuity arrangements.

Insurance

ISEA may maintain insurance appropriate to its activities and risk exposure, having regard to:

the nature and scale of operations;

contractual requirements;

legal and regulatory considerations;

financial resources; and

the cost and availability of appropriate coverage.

Insurance shall not be treated as a substitute for appropriate risk controls.

Third-Party and Outsourcing Risk

Before appointing significant external service providers, ISEA shall consider relevant risks arising from the proposed relationship.

Where proportionate, ISEA may assess:

financial and operational capability;

information security and privacy controls;

legal and regulatory compliance;

reputation;

business continuity;

concentration risk;

contractual protections; and

dependence on critical suppliers.

Significant outsourced activities shall be monitored appropriately.

Risk Culture and Training

ISEA shall promote a risk-aware culture in which persons responsible for ISEA activities understand their responsibilities for identifying and escalating material risks.

ISEA may provide training or guidance concerning:

risk identification;

information security;

privacy;

fraud prevention;

conflicts of interest;

professional and ethical obligations;

business continuity; and

other risk-management matters relevant to particular roles.

Individuals shall not be penalised for raising legitimate concerns about material risks in good faith through appropriate channels.

Responsibilities

17.1 Governing Council

The Governing Council has ultimate responsibility for overseeing ISEA's risk-management framework.

The Governing Council shall:

approve this Policy;

establish or approve ISEA's overall risk appetite;

oversee material and strategic risks;

receive appropriate risk reporting;

ensure appropriate risk-management arrangements are maintained; and

review significant risk matters requiring Governing Council attention.

17.2 Audit, Risk and Compliance Committee

Where established, the Audit, Risk and Compliance Committee shall support the Governing Council by:

monitoring the effectiveness of the risk-management framework;

reviewing significant risks and mitigation measures;

reviewing material incidents and emerging risks;

monitoring financial, compliance and operational risk matters; and

recommending improvements to the Governing Council.

17.3 Management and Executives

Management and executives are responsible for implementing approved risk-management arrangements within their areas of responsibility.

They shall:

identify and manage material risks;

maintain appropriate controls;

report material risk developments;

implement mitigation measures; and

ensure relevant staff and volunteers understand their responsibilities.

17.4 Committees and Other Responsible Persons

Committees, officers, employees, volunteers and representatives are responsible for identifying and appropriately managing risks within their areas of responsibility and escalating material matters through appropriate channels.

Risk Monitoring and Review

ISEA shall periodically review its material risks and the effectiveness of relevant controls.

Monitoring may include:

review of risk-register entries;

key risk indicators;

incident trends;

control assessments;

audit findings;

regulatory developments;

stakeholder feedback; and

emerging-risk analysis.

Material changes in the risk environment shall be communicated to the appropriate governance body.

Relationship with Other ISEA Policies

This Policy should be read together with other ISEA policies, regulations and procedures relevant to risk management, including:

Ethics Policy;

Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct;

Conflict of Interest Policy;

Privacy Policy;

Document Retention Policy;

Complaints Policy;

Disciplinary Policy;

Whistleblower Policy;

Membership Policy;

Membership Regulations;

Member Admission Framework; and

Continuing Professional Development Policy.

Where another ISEA policy establishes specific requirements for managing a particular risk, those requirements shall apply in conjunction with this Policy.

Breaches

Failure to comply with this Policy may result in corrective action, management action or disciplinary action, as appropriate and in accordance with applicable ISEA policies and procedures.

Conduct involving dishonesty, concealment, deliberate misrepresentation, obstruction, misuse of information or other serious misconduct may also constitute a breach of the ISEA Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct.

Review and Continuous Improvement

This Policy shall be reviewed periodically by the Audit, Risk and Compliance Committee, or such other body as the Governing Council may designate.

The review shall consider:

changes in ISEA's activities and operating environment;

significant incidents and lessons learned;

changes in legal or regulatory requirements;

technological developments, including artificial intelligence;

emerging risks;

changes in ISEA's strategic objectives; and

the effectiveness of existing risk controls.

Amendments to this Policy shall be subject to approval by the Governing Council.

Effective Date

This Risk Management Policy takes effect on the date approved by the ISEA Governing Council.

Governance Document
Governance Policy

Volunteer and Committee Policy

International Society of Equity Analysts

DOCUMENT VERSION 1.2 DATE APPROVED 1 July 2025
LAST UPDATED 1 July 2026 ADMINISTERED BY Membership and Chapters Committee
This document forms part of the official governance framework of the International Society of Equity Analysts (ISEA) and should be read together with the related documents listed above.

Purpose

The International Society of Equity Analysts (“ISEA”) relies on the voluntary contribution of time, expertise and judgement of its Governing Council members, committee members, working group members, taskforce members and other volunteers in the governance, administration and delivery of its professional, educational, membership and standard-setting activities.

This Volunteer and Committee Policy (“Policy”) establishes the framework governing the appointment, responsibilities, conduct, confidentiality obligations, conflicts of interest, expenses, indemnity, reporting obligations, removal and cessation of appointment of ISEA volunteers and committee members.

This Policy is intended to ensure that ISEA’s committees and volunteer structures operate consistently, transparently and in a manner that protects the integrity of ISEA, its Members, its governance processes and the wider equity analysis profession.

This Policy supports ISEA’s Charter and operates alongside other ISEA policies, including the Ethics Policy, the Conflict of Interest Policy, the Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct, the Whistleblower Policy, the Disciplinary Policy and applicable Committee Charters.

Nothing in this Policy limits or overrides the powers and functions of the Governing Council under the Charter, or the specific terms of any Committee Charter approved by the Governing Council. Where a conflict arises between this Policy and a Committee Charter, the Governing Council shall determine which provision prevails, having regard to the Charter.

Scope and Application

This Policy applies to:

Governing Council members, including the Chair and Vice-Chair of the Governing Council

Committee members, including chairs, vice-chairs and ordinary members of all standing, ad hoc, advisory and special-purpose committees established by ISEA

Working group and taskforce members convened under the authority of the Governing Council or a committee

Volunteers who assist ISEA in any capacity, including chapter or regional representatives, mentors, examiners, moderators, event volunteers and subject-matter reviewers and

Officers and representatives appointed by ISEA to represent it in an external forum, working party, regulatory consultation or industry body,

(each, an “Appointee”, and collectively “Appointees”).

This Policy applies from the date an individual accepts an appointment, nomination or invitation referred to above, and continues to apply, where relevant, following cessation of that appointment in accordance with the surviving obligations described in this Policy (including confidentiality and conflicts obligations).

This Policy does not apply to ISEA employees engaged under a contract of employment, whose conduct, appointment and remuneration are governed by their employment terms and applicable ISEA human resources policies, provided that an employee who additionally serves on a committee or as a volunteer in a personal capacity is subject to this Policy in that capacity.

This Policy should be read together with the specific Committee Charter applicable to each committee, which may impose additional or more specific requirements relating to that committee’s composition, quorum, voting and decision-making procedures.

Definitions and Interpretation

In this Policy, unless the context otherwise requires:

“Appointee” has the meaning given in clause 2

“Chair” means the individual appointed to preside over a committee, working group or taskforce

“Committee” means any standing, ad hoc, advisory or special-purpose body established by the Governing Council or under a Committee Charter, and includes working groups and taskforces unless the context indicates otherwise

“Committee Charter” means the charter or terms of reference approved by the Governing Council for a particular committee

“Confidential Information” has the meaning given in clause 8

“Executive Secretariat” means the Secretary-General and the administrative staff of ISEA who support the Governing Council and its committees

“Governing Council” means the governing body of ISEA established under the Charter

“Immediate Family” means a spouse or domestic partner, parent, child, sibling, and any other relative who resides in the same household as an Appointee

“Member” means a Student Member, Associate Member, Member (MISEA) or Fellow (FISEA) of ISEA

“Secretary-General” means the person holding that office within ISEA’s Executive Secretariat from time to time and

“Volunteer” means an individual described in clause 2 who is not a Governing Council member or committee member but who otherwise assists ISEA in a voluntary, unremunerated or honorarium-based capacity.

Headings are for convenience only and do not affect interpretation. A reference to a policy, framework or Charter includes that document as amended, replaced or superseded from time to time. Words importing the singular include the plural and vice versa.

Governance Structure of Committees

4.1 Types of Committees

ISEA’s committee structure may include, without limitation, standing committees (established on an ongoing basis to support core governance or professional functions), advisory committees (established to provide expert or stakeholder input), regional or chapter committees (established to support Members within a defined geography), and ad hoc committees, working groups or taskforces (established for a defined purpose or period).

The Governing Council determines the committee structure of ISEA from time to time and may, at its discretion, establish, merge, restructure or dissolve any committee.

4.2 Establishment and Discontinuation of Committees

A committee is established by resolution of the Governing Council, which shall approve the committee’s Committee Charter, including its purpose, composition, reporting lines and, where applicable, its budget and delegated authority.

A committee may be discontinued by resolution of the Governing Council where its purpose has been fulfilled, is no longer required, or where discontinuation is otherwise in the interests of ISEA. Discontinuation does not, of itself, extinguish any surviving obligations of former committee members under this Policy.

4.3 Committee Charters

Each committee shall operate under a Committee Charter approved by the Governing Council, which shall be consistent with this Policy and shall specify, at a minimum, the committee’s objectives, scope of authority, composition and quorum requirements, meeting frequency, and reporting obligations to the Governing Council.

Where a Committee Charter is silent on a matter addressed by this Policy, this Policy shall apply.

Appointment of Committee Members and Volunteers

5.1 Eligibility Criteria

Unless otherwise specified in the relevant Committee Charter, an individual is eligible for appointment as a committee member or volunteer if the individual:

holds current Membership of ISEA at the relevant Membership grade specified for the role, where Membership is a stated requirement of that role

is not currently suspended or expelled from ISEA Membership, and has no unresolved disciplinary matter that the Governing Council considers relevant to the appointment

has disclosed any actual, potential or perceived conflicts of interest relevant to the role in accordance with clause 7 and

has the relevant skills, experience, availability and, where applicable, independence appropriate to the role.

The Governing Council or the relevant committee, as applicable, may adopt additional eligibility criteria for particular roles, including requirements relating to geographic or sectoral representation, diversity of perspective, or professional designation.

5.2 Nomination and Selection Process

Appointments to committees and volunteer roles shall be made through a nomination and selection process determined by the Governing Council or the relevant committee, which may include open calls for expressions of interest, nomination by existing committee members, or invitation by the Secretary-General.

Selection decisions shall have regard to the eligibility criteria in clause 5.1, the needs of the committee, and, where applicable, the desirability of maintaining an appropriate diversity of professional background, geography, gender and seniority across ISEA’s committee structure.

An appointment takes effect only upon written confirmation by the Secretary-General or the relevant committee Chair, and upon the appointee’s written acknowledgement of, and agreement to comply with, this Policy and any other applicable ISEA requirements.

5.3 Terms of Appointment

Unless otherwise specified in the relevant Committee Charter, appointments to a committee are for a term of one (1) year, renewable for no more than two further consecutive terms, after which a period of at least one (1) year must elapse before the individual is eligible for re-appointment to the same committee, unless the Governing Council determines that an exception is warranted having regard to continuity, expertise or succession considerations.

The Governing Council may stagger the terms of committee members to preserve continuity of institutional knowledge within a committee.

5.4 Induction and Onboarding

The Executive Secretariat shall provide each newly appointed committee member and volunteer with an induction covering, at a minimum, the applicable Committee Charter, this Policy, the Ethics Policy, the Conflict of Interest Policy, the Confidentiality obligations in clause 8, and any specific procedural or reporting requirements relevant to the role.

5.5 Re-appointment

Re-appointment at the end of a term is not automatic. The Governing Council or relevant committee shall have regard to the individual’s attendance, contribution, conduct and continued eligibility when considering re-appointment.

Roles and Responsibilities

6.1 General Responsibilities of Committee Members and Volunteers

Committee members and volunteers shall:

act honestly, in good faith and in the best interests of ISEA and its Members as a whole, rather than in the interests of any particular constituency, employer, sponsor or personal interest

exercise reasonable care, skill and diligence in performing their role

attend and participate constructively in meetings and, where unable to attend, provide reasonable advance notice to the Chair or Secretariat

familiarise themselves with, and comply with, the applicable Committee Charter, this Policy and other applicable ISEA policies and

act within the scope of authority delegated to the relevant committee and refrain from making representations on behalf of ISEA beyond that scope without proper authorisation.

6.2 Responsibilities of Committee Chairs

In addition to the responsibilities in clause 6.1, a committee Chair is responsible for providing leadership to the committee, setting agendas in consultation with the Secretariat, ensuring balanced participation among committee members, escalating matters requiring Governing Council attention, and ensuring the committee reports to the Governing Council in accordance with clause 13.

A committee Chair should ensure that meetings are conducted efficiently, that dissenting views are appropriately recorded, and that decisions are made in accordance with the quorum and voting requirements set out in the relevant Committee Charter.

6.3 Responsibilities of the Secretary-General and Executive Secretariat

The Secretary-General and Executive Secretariat provide administrative and governance support to committees, including scheduling meetings, distributing papers, maintaining minutes and records in accordance with the Document Retention Policy, and supporting the induction, appointment and, where relevant, removal processes described in this Policy.

6.4 Time Commitment and Attendance

Committee members and volunteers are expected to commit sufficient time to fulfil their role effectively, including preparation for and attendance at meetings. A committee member who is absent, without reasonable excuse, from more than half of a committee’s scheduled meetings within a twelve-month period may be treated as having resigned in accordance with clause 10.3, subject to the Chair first raising the matter with the individual concerned.

Conflicts of Interest

7.1 Identification of Conflicts

Committee members and volunteers must proactively identify circumstances in which their personal, professional, financial or other interests, or those of their employer, clients or Immediate Family, could conflict, or could reasonably be perceived to conflict, with their duties to ISEA.

A conflict of interest may arise, for example, where a matter before a committee could affect the commercial interests of the Appointee’s employer, where the Appointee has a financial interest in the outcome of a decision, or where the Appointee’s objectivity could reasonably be questioned because of a personal or professional relationship with a person affected by the matter.

7.2 Disclosure Obligations

Committee members and volunteers must disclose actual, potential or perceived conflicts of interest to the Chair of the relevant committee (or, in the case of the Chair’s own conflict, to the Secretary-General) as soon as practicable, and in any event before participating in the discussion or decision to which the conflict relates.

Disclosures must be recorded in the minutes of the relevant meeting and in the register of interests described in clause 7.4.

7.3 Management of Conflicts

On disclosure of a conflict, the Chair (or, where the conflict concerns the Chair, the Vice-Chair or another committee member nominated by the Secretary-General) shall determine the appropriate management response, which may include requiring the Appointee to:

refrain from participating in the discussion of the relevant matter

withdraw from the meeting, or the relevant part of the meeting, during consideration of the matter

abstain from voting on the matter or

in serious or recurring cases, step down from the committee in relation to matters of that kind, or from the committee altogether.

This clause 7 operates in addition to, and does not limit, the requirements of ISEA’s Conflict of Interest Policy, which shall prevail to the extent of any inconsistency.

7.4 Register of Interests

The Executive Secretariat shall maintain a register of interests recording disclosures made under this clause 7. Committee members and volunteers must update their disclosures promptly upon any material change in circumstances, and in any event review and confirm their disclosures on an annual basis.

Confidentiality and Information Handling

8.1 General Confidentiality Obligations

In the course of their appointment, committee members and volunteers may have access to information that is not publicly available, including draft policies, deliberations of the Governing Council or a committee, Member complaints or disciplinary matters, examination materials, financial information, and information provided in confidence by Members, applicants or third parties (“Confidential Information”).

Committee members and volunteers must not disclose Confidential Information to any third party, or use Confidential Information for any purpose other than the proper performance of their role, except:

with the prior written authorisation of the Secretary-General or the Governing Council

where disclosure is required by law, regulation or a valid order of a court or regulator, in which case the individual should, where legally permitted, notify the Secretary-General before making the disclosure or

where the information has already lawfully entered the public domain other than through a breach of this clause.

8.2 Use and Protection of Confidential Information

Committee members and volunteers must take reasonable steps to protect Confidential Information from unauthorised access, including by using ISEA-approved systems for storing and transmitting committee materials where these are made available, and by not retaining Confidential Information beyond the period reasonably necessary for the performance of their role.

Committee deliberations, including differing views expressed during discussion, are confidential to the committee unless and until a decision or communication is formally approved for release.

8.3 Continuing Obligations After Cessation

The obligations in this clause 8 survive the cessation of an individual’s appointment for any reason, and continue to apply for so long as the relevant information remains confidential.

Standards of Conduct

9.1 General Standards

Committee members and volunteers must at all times comply with the Ethics Policy and the Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct, and must otherwise conduct themselves in a manner consistent with ISEA’s reputation for integrity and professionalism, including in their interactions with

Members, ISEA staff, other Appointees and external stakeholders.

Committee members and volunteers must not engage in conduct that is discriminatory, harassing, bullying or otherwise inconsistent with a respectful and inclusive working environment.

9.2 Use of ISEA Resources, Name and Brand

Committee members and volunteers must use ISEA resources, including its name, logo, letterhead and confidential systems, only for purposes properly connected with their role, and must not use ISEA’s name or brand to endorse, or appear to endorse, any commercial product, service or organisation without the prior written approval of the Secretary-General.

9.3 External Communications and Social Media

Committee members and volunteers must not make public statements, including on social media, on behalf of ISEA unless authorised to do so, and should make clear, where they comment publicly on matters relevant to ISEA in a personal capacity, that the views expressed are their own and not those of ISEA.

9.4 Gifts, Benefits and Hospitality

Committee members and volunteers must not solicit, and should decline or refer to the Secretary-General, any gift, benefit or hospitality offered in connection with their role that could reasonably be perceived to influence, or to be intended to influence, the performance of their duties, other than benefits of modest, customary or nominal value.

Resignation, Removal and Cessation of Appointment

10.1 Resignation

A committee member or volunteer may resign at any time by giving written notice to the Chair of the relevant committee or to the Secretary-General. Except in urgent circumstances, at least thirty days’ notice should be given to allow for an orderly handover.

10.2 Removal for Cause

The Governing Council may remove a committee member or volunteer from their appointment at any time, with or without notice, where the individual:

has breached this Policy, the applicable Committee Charter, the Ethics Policy or the Code

has failed, without reasonable excuse, to meet the standards of attendance, participation or conduct expected of the role

has an unmanageable or undisclosed conflict of interest

has ceased to meet the eligibility criteria for the role, including through suspension or expulsion from ISEA Membership or

is, in the reasonable opinion of the Governing Council, no longer able to perform the role effectively or in a manner consistent with ISEA’s interests.

Save in urgent cases or cases involving a serious breach, an individual subject to potential removal should be given a reasonable opportunity to respond before a final decision is made. A decision to remove a committee member or volunteer, and the reasons for it, shall be recorded by the Executive Secretariat.

10.3 Automatic Cessation

An individual’s appointment ceases automatically, without the need for further action by the Governing Council, upon the expiry of their term (unless renewed in accordance with clause 5.3), upon the individual’s death, or upon the individual otherwise ceasing to satisfy a mandatory eligibility requirement of the role specified in the applicable Committee Charter.

10.4 Effect of Cessation

On cessation of an appointment for any reason, the individual must promptly return or destroy all ISEA materials and Confidential Information in their possession, cease to represent themselves as holding the relevant role, and remains bound by the confidentiality and conflicts obligations described in clauses 7 and 8 to the extent they survive cessation.

Expenses and Reimbursement

11.1 General Principles

Committee members and volunteers serve in a voluntary capacity and are not remunerated for their time unless the Governing Council determines otherwise for a specific role. ISEA will, however, reimburse reasonable, properly incurred and pre-approved expenses in accordance with this clause 11 and any expense guidelines issued by the Executive Secretariat from time to time.

11.2 Eligible Expenses

Subject to prior approval and any applicable expense guidelines, eligible expenses may include reasonable travel, accommodation and subsistence costs incurred in attending in-person committee meetings or representing ISEA at an authorised event, and other direct out-of-pocket costs reasonably and necessarily incurred in the performance of the role.

Expenses should be incurred economically, having regard to ISEA’s status as a not-for-profit professional association, and business or premium-class travel will only be reimbursed in limited circumstances approved in advance by the Secretary-General.

11.3 Claims Process

Claims for reimbursement must be submitted to the Executive Secretariat in the form and within the timeframe specified in ISEA’s expense guidelines, supported by original receipts or other satisfactory evidence of expenditure. Claims submitted more than ninety days after the expense was incurred may be declined at ISEA’s discretion.

11.4 Non-Reimbursable Expenses

ISEA will not reimburse expenses that are not properly connected with an individual’s role, expenses incurred without required pre-approval, fines or penalties, or expenses that would give rise to a conflict of interest or the appearance of impropriety.

Indemnity and Limitation of Liability

12.1 Indemnity

Subject to applicable law and ISEA’s Charter, ISEA shall indemnify each Governing Council member and committee member, out of the assets of ISEA, against liability reasonably incurred by that individual in connection with the proper performance of their role, including reasonable legal costs, provided that the individual acted honestly, in good faith and within the scope of their authority, and did not act fraudulently, with wilful misconduct, or in a manner constituting a serious or knowing breach of this Policy.

This indemnity does not extend to liability arising from an individual’s fraud, dishonesty, wilful default, gross negligence, or knowing breach of applicable law or ISEA policy.

12.2 Limitation of Liability

To the maximum extent permitted by applicable law, no committee member or volunteer shall be personally liable for any act or omission done in good faith in the proper performance of their role, and any liability that would otherwise attach to the individual shall, to that extent, attach instead to ISEA.

12.3 Insurance

ISEA shall maintain directors’ and officers’ liability insurance, or equivalent cover, for the benefit of Governing Council members and committee members, in such amount and on such terms as the Governing Council considers appropriate from time to time, and shall provide committee members with reasonable information as to the scope of that cover on request.

Committee Reporting and Accountability

13.1 Reporting to the Governing Council

Each committee shall report to the Governing Council in accordance with the frequency and format specified in its Committee Charter, and in any event at least once per year, covering the committee’s activities, key decisions, matters escalated for the Governing Council’s attention, and any material risks or conflicts identified.

A committee Chair, or the Secretary-General on the Chair’s behalf, shall promptly escalate to the Governing Council any matter that could materially affect ISEA’s reputation, financial position or legal or regulatory standing.

13.2 Minutes and Records

Minutes of committee meetings shall be prepared by, or under the supervision of, the Executive Secretariat, circulated to committee members for review within a reasonable period, and retained in accordance with the Document Retention Policy. Minutes shall record attendance, key discussion points, decisions taken, dissenting views (where a member requests this), and any conflict of interest disclosures made under clause 7.

13.3 Performance Review

The Governing Council may, from time to time, review the performance and continued relevance of a committee, including through self-assessment by committee members, feedback from Members, or an independent review, and may make recommendations arising from that review, including as to the committee’s composition, mandate or continuation.

Review and Continuous Improvement

This Policy shall be reviewed by the Governing Council periodically, and in any event at least once every three years, to ensure that it remains fit for purpose, consistent with applicable law and regulation, and aligned with good governance practice among comparable international professional associations.

The Governing Council may also review this Policy earlier than scheduled where prompted by a material change in ISEA’s governance structure, a lesson identified through the operation of a committee, feedback from committee members, Members or other stakeholders, or a relevant legal or regulatory development.

The Secretary-General is responsible for monitoring the effectiveness of this Policy in practice and for bringing recommendations for improvement to the Governing Council.

Effective Date

This Policy takes effect from the date of its approval by the Governing Council and remains in effect until amended, replaced or withdrawn by a further resolution of the Governing Council.

Governance Document
Governance Policy

Whistleblower Policy

International Society of Equity Analysts

DOCUMENT VERSION 1.0 DATE APPROVED 1 July 2026
LAST UPDATED 1 July 2026 ADMINISTERED BY Executive Committee
This document forms part of the official governance framework of the International Society of Equity Analysts (ISEA) and should be read together with the related documents listed above.

Purpose

The International Society of Equity Analysts (ISEA) is committed to maintaining the highest standards of integrity, accountability, transparency, and ethical conduct across all aspects of its operations.

This Whistleblower Policy establishes a framework to encourage and protect individuals who, in good faith, report concerns regarding suspected misconduct, unethical behaviour, breaches of law, breaches of ISEA policies, professional standards violations, fraud, corruption, conflicts of interest, or conduct that may harm ISEA, its members, investors, or the broader equity analysis profession.

ISEA recognises that individuals who identify wrongdoing may face concerns regarding confidentiality, retaliation, or professional consequences. This Policy is designed to provide a safe, confidential, and fair process for raising concerns and ensuring that appropriate action is taken.

This Policy operates consistently with the Ethics Policy, Conflict of Interest Policy, Complaints Policy, Disciplinary Policy, and the ethical principles contained in the Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct (“Code”).

Scope and Application

This Policy applies to:

Governing Council members;

Officers and executives;

Committee members;

Employees;

Members (Student Members, Associate Members, Members and Fellows);

Certification holders;

Candidates;

Volunteers;

Contractors;

Consultants;

Education providers;

Partners;

Any person performing services for or representing ISEA.

A person making a disclosure under this Policy is referred to as a Whistleblower.

Purpose of Whistleblower Protection

ISEA seeks to create an environment where individuals are encouraged to raise legitimate concerns without fear of:

Retaliation;

Victimisation;

Discrimination;

Harassment;

Professional disadvantage;

Unfair treatment.

ISEA considers responsible reporting of wrongdoing to be an important contribution to maintaining professional standards and organisational integrity.

Matters That May Be Reported

A Whistleblower may raise concerns regarding actual, suspected, or potential misconduct, including:

4.1 Fraud and Financial Misconduct

Including:

Fraudulent activity;

Theft or misuse of ISEA resources;

Financial misreporting;

Improper financial transactions;

Corruption or bribery.

4.2 Ethical and Professional Misconduct

Including:

Breaches of the ISEA Ethics Policy;

Breaches of the CFA Institute Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct;

Misrepresentation of qualifications or certifications;

Dishonest professional conduct;

Research integrity concerns.

4.3 Conflicts of Interest

Including:

Undisclosed conflicts;

Improper personal benefit;

Abuse of position;

Failure to act independently.

4.4 Governance and Leadership Concerns

Including:

Misconduct by Governing Council members, officers, or committee members;

Abuse of authority;

Breaches of fiduciary responsibilities;

Failure of governance processes.

4.5 Legal and Regulatory Breaches

Including:

Breaches of applicable laws;

Regulatory misconduct;

Conduct likely to cause harm to members, investors, or the public.

4.6 Other Serious Misconduct

Including conduct that may:

Damage ISEA’s reputation;

Undermine professional standards;

Compromise member trust;

Harm the integrity of the equity analysis profession.

Matters Generally Not Covered

This Policy is not intended primarily for:

General membership complaints;

Service dissatisfaction;

Personal disputes;

Routine administrative matters.

Such matters may be addressed under the Complaints Policy.

However, a matter initially submitted as a complaint may be treated as a whistleblower disclosure where it involves serious misconduct or public interest concerns.

Good Faith Reporting

ISEA encourages individuals to report concerns honestly and responsibly.

A person does not need to prove that misconduct has occurred before making a disclosure. A reasonable belief that misconduct may have occurred is sufficient.

A Whistleblower should provide:

A description of the concern;

Relevant facts;

Names of persons involved, where known;

Supporting evidence or information;

Any relevant dates or circumstances.

Protection Against Retaliation

ISEA prohibits retaliation against any person who:

Makes a disclosure in good faith;

Assists with an investigation;

Provides information relating to suspected misconduct;

Participates in a whistleblower process.

Retaliation includes:

Threats;

Harassment;

Discrimination;

Removal from opportunities;

Unfair treatment;

Professional disadvantage.

Any person engaging in retaliation may be subject to disciplinary action.

Confidentiality and Anonymity

ISEA will protect the confidentiality of Whistleblowers to the greatest extent reasonably possible.

Information relating to a disclosure will only be shared with persons who:

Need the information to assess or investigate the matter;

Are responsible for governance oversight;

Are required by law to receive the information.

ISEA may accept anonymous disclosures where sufficient information is provided to allow meaningful assessment.

Where anonymity is maintained, ISEA may be limited in its ability to:

Seek further information;

Provide updates;

Conduct a complete investigation.

Reporting Channels

Concerns may be reported through appropriate channels established by ISEA.

Reports may be submitted to:

The Chairperson of the Audit, Risk and Compliance Committee;

The Chairperson of the Ethics and Professional Standards Committee;

The ISEA Governing Council Chairperson;

An independent reporting channel designated by ISEA.

Where the concern relates to a particular person, the disclosure should be directed to a person independent of that individual.

Assessment of Disclosures

Upon receiving a disclosure, ISEA shall undertake an initial assessment to determine:

Whether the matter falls within this Policy;

Whether urgent action is required;

Whether an investigation should commence;

Whether another process is more appropriate.

Possible outcomes include:

No further action;

Referral to another ISEA process;

Informal resolution;

Formal investigation.

Investigation Process

Where an investigation is required, ISEA may:

Appoint an investigator;

Establish an independent review panel;

Examine relevant documents;

Interview relevant persons;

Obtain expert advice;

Consult professional advisers.

Investigations shall be conducted:

Objectively;

Confidentially;

Fairly;

Without predetermined conclusions.

Rights of Persons Named in Disclosures

Individuals who are the subject of a disclosure shall be treated fairly.

They shall generally be:

Informed of allegations where appropriate;

Given an opportunity to respond;

Provided procedural fairness.

ISEA may delay notification where necessary to protect:

Evidence;

The integrity of the investigation;

The confidentiality of the Whistleblower.

Investigation Outcomes

Following investigation, ISEA may determine that:

The concern is unsubstantiated;

Further monitoring is appropriate;

Remedial action is required;

Policy improvements are necessary;

Disciplinary action should commence;

External referral is appropriate.

Where appropriate, findings may be referred to:

The Ethics and Professional Standards Committee;

The Audit, Risk and Compliance Committee;

The Governing Council;

Regulators or authorities.

Responsibilities

14.1 Whistleblowers

Whistleblowers are expected to:

Act honestly and in good faith;

Provide accurate information;

Maintain confidentiality where requested;

Cooperate with reasonable investigation processes.

14.2 Governing Council

The Governing Council is responsible for:

Ensuring appropriate whistleblower governance;

Protecting organisational integrity;

Overseeing significant matters.

14.3 Audit, Risk and Compliance Committee

The Audit, Risk and Compliance Committee shall:

Oversee whistleblower arrangements;

Monitor significant disclosures;

Ensure appropriate investigation processes;

Report material matters to the Governing Council.

14.4 Ethics and Professional Standards Committee

The Ethics and Professional Standards Committee shall:

Address ethical misconduct matters;

Consider professional standards breaches;

Recommend disciplinary action where appropriate.

Malicious or False Reports

ISEA recognises that disclosures made in good faith should be protected even where concerns are ultimately unsubstantiated.

However, knowingly false, malicious, or deliberately misleading reports may constitute misconduct and may result in disciplinary action.

Records and Reporting

ISEA shall maintain appropriate records regarding:

Disclosures received;

Assessments conducted;

Investigations undertaken;

Outcomes achieved;

Remedial actions implemented.

Material whistleblower matters shall be reported to the Governing Council while protecting confidentiality.

Relationship with Other ISEA Policies

This Policy should be read together with:

Ethics Policy;

Code;

Conflict of Interest Policy;

Complaints Policy;

Disciplinary Policy;

Privacy Policy;

Risk Management Policy;

Risk Management Framework.

Review and Continuous Improvement

The Audit, Risk & Compliance Committee shall periodically review this Policy to ensure alignment with:

Applicable whistleblower laws;

Governance best practices;

Professional standards;

Organisational developments.

The Committee shall recommend amendments to the Governing Council where appropriate.

Effective Date

This Whistleblower Policy takes effect on the date approved by the ISEA Governing Council.

Governance Document
Governance Policy

Workplace Health, Safety and Wellbeing Policy

International Society of Equity Analysts

DOCUMENT VERSION 1.2 DATE APPROVED 1 July 2025
LAST UPDATED 1 July 2026 ADMINISTERED BY Committee
This document forms part of the official governance framework of the International Society of Equity Analysts (ISEA) and should be read together with the related documents listed above.

Purpose

The International Society of Equity Analysts (“ISEA”) is committed to providing and maintaining a safe, healthy environment for everyone who works for, volunteers with, contracts with, or participates in the activities of ISEA, wherever in the world those activities take place.

As a large, multinational professional association, ISEA maintains offices, employs staff, engages contractors and volunteers, and organises conferences, examinations and chapter events across many jurisdictions. Each of these settings carries distinct health and safety considerations, and ISEA recognises its responsibility to identify, assess and manage the risks associated with each.

This Workplace Health, Safety and Wellbeing Policy (“Policy”) sets out ISEA’s commitment to protecting the physical and psychological health, safety and wellbeing of its employees, offices, event and conference participants, volunteers and contractors, and establishes the principles, responsibilities and processes by which that commitment is implemented.

ISEA regards health, safety and wellbeing not merely as a compliance obligation, but as a fundamental element of responsible organisational governance and as a precondition for a professional community in which people can do their best work and participate fully in ISEA’s mission.

This Policy operates alongside, and should be read together with, ISEA’s Ethics Policy, Equality, Diversity and Inclusion Policy, Risk Management Policy and other applicable ISEA policies and governance requirements.

Scope and Application

This Policy applies to:

employees of ISEA, wherever based, including those working from an ISEA office, remotely, or on a hybrid basis;

the Secretary-General and members of the Executive Secretariat;

Governing Council members, officers and committee members, in connection with ISEA governance activities;

volunteers, examiners, assessors, mentors, speakers and other representatives acting on behalf of ISEA;

contractors, consultants, secondees and agency staff engaged by ISEA;

ISEA Members and other attendees participating in ISEA-organised or ISEA-sanctioned conferences, examinations, chapter meetings and events; and

visitors to ISEA offices and premises.

This Policy applies to ISEA offices and premises, ISEA-organised or ISEA-sanctioned events, conferences and examinations, business travel undertaken in connection with ISEA activities, and, in relation to psychological health and wellbeing, to ISEA-related conduct occurring through digital platforms and remote working arrangements.

Because ISEA operates in many jurisdictions, this Policy is intended to establish a consistent minimum standard across ISEA’s global operations, reflecting internationally recognised occupational health and safety principles. Where local law imposes a higher or more specific standard than this Policy in the jurisdiction in which an ISEA office, event or activity is located, the local legal standard shall apply in addition to this Policy. Nothing in this Policy is intended to require, or to excuse compliance with, conduct that would breach applicable local law.

This Policy does not form part of, and does not vary, any contract of employment or engagement. Employment-related occupational health and safety matters will additionally be governed by applicable local law and any separate ISEA human resources policies and procedures.

Definitions

For the purposes of this Policy:

“Hazard” means a source or situation with the potential to cause harm to a person’s health or safety, whether physical or psychological.

“Risk” means the likelihood and potential severity of harm arising from exposure to a Hazard.

“Incident” means an unplanned event that resulted in, or had the potential to result in, injury, illness, property damage or other loss, including a “near miss” where no actual harm occurred.

“Duty of Care” means ISEA’s responsibility to take reasonable steps to protect the health, safety and wellbeing of persons affected by its activities.

“Workplace” means any location where ISEA-related work or activity is performed, including ISEA offices, remote and home working locations, event and conference venues, and locations visited in the course of ISEA-related business travel.

“Wellbeing” means a person’s physical, psychological and social state of being, encompassing both the absence of harm and the presence of factors that support health, resilience and a positive working environment.

“Lone Working” means work carried out by a person without close or direct supervision, or without another person present, whether at an ISEA office, a remote location, or in the course of business travel.

“Fitness for Role” means a person’s physical and psychological capacity to safely and effectively perform the specific duties of their role or activity.

“HSW Committee” means the Health, Safety and Wellbeing Committee established under Section 5 of this Policy.

Policy Statement and Commitment

ISEA is committed to:

providing and maintaining a safe and healthy working environment across its offices, events and other activities, so far as is reasonably practicable;

identifying, assessing and managing health and safety risks associated with ISEA’s premises, events, travel and operations;

consulting with employees, volunteers and other stakeholders on matters affecting their health, safety and wellbeing;

providing information, instruction, training and supervision necessary to enable people to carry out ISEA-related activities safely;

promoting positive psychological health and wellbeing, and providing appropriate support to those experiencing work-related stress or other health and wellbeing difficulties;

investigating incidents and near misses, and taking corrective action to prevent recurrence;

complying with applicable health and safety law in each jurisdiction in which ISEA operates; and

continually improving its health, safety and wellbeing performance over time.

This commitment applies equally to ISEA’s treatment of its employees and to the safety of volunteers, contractors, Members and other participants in ISEA activities, recognising that ISEA’s duty of care extends beyond its direct workforce to all those who engage with ISEA’s offices, events and operations.

Governance and Oversight

ISEA shall maintain a Health, Safety and Wellbeing (HSW) Committee, reporting to the Governing Council, responsible for overseeing the implementation, monitoring and continuous improvement of this Policy. Until decided otherwise by the Governing Council, the HSW Committee shall be the Executive Secretariat.

The HSW Committee’s responsibilities may include:

advising the Governing Council on ISEA’s health, safety and wellbeing strategy, priorities and resourcing;

reviewing significant incidents, hazards and risk assessments arising from ISEA offices, events and operations;

monitoring compliance with this Policy and applicable health and safety law across ISEA’s offices and jurisdictions;

reviewing event and conference risk assessments for higher-risk activities;

recommending health, safety and wellbeing training, resources and initiatives; and

recommending amendments to this Policy in accordance with Section 28.

The HSW Committee shall work closely with the Executive Secretariat, which retains day-to-day operational responsibility for health and safety management, and shall liaise, where relevant, with the Ethics & Professional Standards Committee, the EDI Committee and the Risk Management function on matters of overlap.

Responsibilities

Maintaining a safe and healthy environment is a shared responsibility across ISEA’s governance, staff, membership, volunteers and contractors.

6.1 Governing Council

The Governing Council is ultimately responsible for approving this Policy, ensuring adequate resourcing for health, safety and wellbeing management, and holding the Executive Secretariat accountable for implementation.

6.2 Secretary-General and Executive Secretariat

The Secretary-General, supported by the Executive Secretariat, is responsible for the day-to-day implementation of this Policy, including maintaining safe offices and systems of work, conducting and reviewing risk assessments, coordinating event and travel safety arrangements, managing incident reporting and investigation, and reporting to the Governing Council and the HSW Committee on health, safety and wellbeing performance.

6.3 Managers and Supervisors

Managers and supervisors are responsible for implementing this Policy within their teams and areas of responsibility, including identifying and addressing hazards, ensuring that employees and contractors under their direction receive necessary training, monitoring workload and wellbeing, and responding appropriately to concerns raised by their teams.

6.4 Employees

Employees are responsible for taking reasonable care of their own health and safety and that of others affected by their acts or omissions, complying with this Policy and related safety instructions, using equipment and facilities properly, reporting hazards and incidents promptly, and cooperating with ISEA’s health and safety measures.

6.5 Volunteers

Volunteers acting on behalf of ISEA, including examiners, assessors, mentors, speakers and chapter volunteers, are responsible for following applicable safety instructions and venue rules, reporting hazards and incidents of which they become aware, and taking reasonable care for their own safety and that of others while engaged in ISEA-related activities.

6.6 Contractors and Suppliers

Contractors, suppliers and venue operators engaged by ISEA are responsible for complying with applicable health and safety law and with any health and safety requirements specified in their engagement, for maintaining safe equipment, premises and systems of work under their control, and for cooperating with ISEA’s health and safety requirements and incident reporting processes.

6.7 Members and Event Attendees

Members and other attendees at ISEA events are expected to comply with venue safety rules and instructions given by ISEA staff, volunteers or venue personnel, to conduct themselves in a manner that does not endanger themselves or others, and to report hazards, incidents or safety concerns to ISEA staff or event organisers.

Office and Workplace Safety

ISEA is committed to maintaining offices and workplaces that are safe, well-maintained and appropriately equipped.

7.1 Workplace Environment

ISEA offices shall be maintained in a clean, orderly condition, with adequate lighting, ventilation, temperature control, and safe means of access and egress. Walkways and fire exits shall be kept clear at all times. Facilities and equipment shall be inspected and maintained in accordance with applicable local requirements and manufacturer guidance.

7.2 Ergonomics and Display Screen Equipment

ISEA will provide employees with workstations, seating and equipment that support good ergonomic practice, and will provide guidance on the safe and comfortable use of display screen equipment, including the importance of appropriate posture, screen positioning and regular breaks. Employees who require an ergonomic assessment or adjustment because of a health condition or disability may request one in accordance with ISEA’s Reasonable Accommodation processes under the Equality, Diversity and Inclusion Policy.

7.3 Fire Safety and Emergency Evacuation

Each ISEA office shall maintain a fire safety plan appropriate to the premises and applicable local law, including clearly marked fire exits and assembly points, working fire detection and, where required, suppression equipment, and periodic fire drills. Office managers are responsible for ensuring that new employees, contractors and visitors are made aware of evacuation procedures.

7.4 Building Security and Access Control

ISEA offices shall maintain appropriate access control and visitor management arrangements, having regard to the nature of the premises and the surrounding environment, to protect the safety of employees, contractors and visitors and the security of ISEA’s premises, records and assets.

7.5 Housekeeping, Equipment and Manual Handling

Employees and contractors shall be provided with guidance on safe manual handling and the safe use of office equipment. Spills, obstructions and other hazards should be reported and addressed promptly. Electrical equipment shall be maintained and inspected in accordance with applicable local requirements.

7.6 Lone Working and Personal Safety

Where an employee, volunteer or contractor is required to work alone at an ISEA office, or otherwise in circumstances of Lone Working, such as opening or closing an office outside normal hours, ISEA will take reasonable steps to assess and manage any associated risk, which may include providing a means of summoning assistance, establishing a check-in arrangement with a colleague or manager, and providing guidance on personal safety appropriate to the location. Employees and volunteers should raise any personal safety concern connected to Lone Working with their manager or the Executive Secretariat.

7.7 Workplace Inspections

ISEA offices shall be subject to periodic health and safety inspection, proportionate to the size and nature of the premises, in order to identify and address hazards before they result in harm. Inspection findings and any resulting corrective actions shall be recorded and tracked to completion.

Remote and Hybrid Working

ISEA recognises that many employees work remotely or on a hybrid basis, and that ISEA’s duty of care extends, so far as is reasonably practicable, to the health and safety of employees working from home or another remote location.

In relation to remote and hybrid working, ISEA will:

provide guidance on setting up a safe and ergonomically appropriate home working environment;

provide, where reasonably practicable, appropriate equipment to support safe remote working, such as suitable seating or display screen equipment;

encourage regular breaks and reasonable boundaries between working and non-working time; and

maintain channels through which remote employees can report hazards, incidents, or health and safety or wellbeing concerns, consistent with those available to office-based employees.

Employees working remotely remain responsible for maintaining a reasonably safe working environment and for promptly reporting any home-working health or safety concern to their manager or the Executive Secretariat.

Event and Conference Safety

ISEA organises and sanctions conferences, examinations, chapter meetings and other events across many jurisdictions, and recognises that these activities carry health and safety considerations distinct from ISEA’s offices.

9.1 Event Risk Assessment

A risk assessment shall be conducted for each significant ISEA-organised event, having regard to factors such as the size and nature of the event, the venue, the profile of attendees, and any specific hazards associated with the format of the event. The risk assessment shall be reviewed and updated where circumstances change materially before the event takes place.

9.2 Venue Selection

Venues for ISEA-organised events shall be selected having regard to their compliance with applicable local safety and building requirements, the adequacy of their fire safety and emergency arrangements, and their physical accessibility, consistent with Section 11.2 of the Equality, Diversity and Inclusion Policy.

9.3 Crowd Management and Capacity

Event organisers shall have regard to venue capacity limits, crowd management arrangements and safe means of entry and egress, particularly for larger conferences and examinations. Attendee numbers shall not be permitted to exceed safe or legally permitted venue capacity.

9.4 Emergency Planning at Events

Event organisers shall ensure that appropriate emergency arrangements are in place for each event, including a means of raising the alarm, clearly communicated evacuation procedures, accessible first aid provision consistent with Section 16, and a nominated person responsible for coordinating the response to an incident or emergency at the event.

9.5 Virtual and Hybrid Events

Where ISEA organises virtual or hybrid events, ISEA will have regard to the digital wellbeing of presenters and attendees, including reasonable scheduling across time zones, and will maintain a means by which participants can report technical or conduct-related concerns arising during the event.

9.6 Speaker, Presenter and Staff Wellbeing

ISEA recognises that employees, volunteers and speakers supporting the delivery of a conference or examination may experience long or irregular working hours around the event. Event organisers should have regard to reasonable rest breaks, adequate staffing levels, and access to food, water and rest facilities for ISEA staff and volunteers working at the event, consistent with the fatigue management principles in Section 13.5.

Business Travel Health and Safety

ISEA recognises that employees, Governing Council members, committee members and, on occasion, volunteers may be required to travel internationally in connection with ISEA business, and that international travel carries health and safety considerations distinct from office-based work.

10.1 Travel Risk Assessment

Before undertaking ISEA-related travel to a higher-risk destination, travellers and the Executive Secretariat shall have regard to relevant government travel advisories, health requirements such as recommended vaccinations, and any specific security or safety considerations applicable to the destination.

10.2 Duty of Care While Travelling

ISEA will take reasonable steps to support the safety of travellers undertaking ISEA business, including maintaining emergency contact arrangements, providing relevant travel and destination information, and, where reasonably practicable and proportionate to the risk profile of the destination, arranging appropriate travel insurance and emergency assistance cover.

10.3 Medical Emergencies and Evacuation

Travellers experiencing a medical emergency while on ISEA business should seek appropriate local medical assistance and notify the Executive Secretariat as soon as reasonably practicable. ISEA will provide reasonable support and assistance, including facilitating access to emergency medical evacuation or repatriation services, where such services are available under applicable travel insurance or emergency assistance arrangements.

Volunteer Health and Safety

ISEA relies significantly on the contribution of volunteers, including examiners, assessors, mentors, chapter leaders and event volunteers, and recognises a duty of care towards them while they are engaged in ISEA-related activities.

In relation to volunteers, ISEA will:

provide volunteers with relevant safety information and instruction appropriate to their role and the activity concerned;

ensure that volunteer roles involving higher-risk activities, if any, are subject to an appropriate risk assessment;

provide volunteers with access to the incident and hazard reporting channels described in Section 17; and

take reasonable steps to ensure that volunteers are not exposed to a materially greater risk than employees performing comparable activities.

Volunteers are encouraged to raise any health and safety concern regarding their role or a specific activity with the relevant committee chair, event organiser or the Executive Secretariat.

Contractor, Supplier and Venue Management

Where ISEA engages contractors, suppliers or venues to deliver services or premises in connection with ISEA activities, ISEA will take reasonable steps, proportionate to the nature and risk profile of the engagement, to:

assess the health and safety competence and track record of significant contractors, suppliers and venues before engagement, where reasonably practicable;

include appropriate health and safety expectations and, where relevant, insurance requirements, in contracts and event agreements;

coordinate health and safety responsibilities where ISEA staff, volunteers or attendees work alongside contractor or venue personnel; and

require contractors and venues to report to ISEA any incident affecting ISEA employees, volunteers, Members or attendees arising from their premises, equipment or services.

This Policy does not itself govern the internal health and safety management systems of independent contractor or venue organisations, which remain responsible for compliance with applicable law, but ISEA will take reasonable and proportionate steps, within its contractual relationships, to promote consistency with the principles of this Policy.

Mental Health and Psychological Wellbeing

ISEA recognises that psychological health and wellbeing are as important as physical health and safety, and is committed to fostering a working environment that supports positive mental health.

13.1 Promoting Positive Mental Health

ISEA will promote awareness of mental health and wellbeing among employees, volunteers and Members, encourage open conversation about mental health without stigma, and provide guidance and resources to support employees experiencing mental health difficulties, consistent with applicable law and the confidentiality principles in Section 23.

13.2 Work-Related Stress and Workload Management

ISEA will take reasonable steps to identify and manage factors that may contribute to excessive or harmful work-related stress, including unsustainable workload, unclear role expectations, and insufficient support or resources. Managers are expected to monitor workload within their teams and to raise concerns with the Executive Secretariat where sustained excessive demands are identified. Employees are encouraged to raise concerns about workload or work-related stress with their manager or through the channels described in Section 17.

13.3 Support Resources

Where reasonably practicable, ISEA will make available or signpost confidential support resources, such as an employee assistance programme, counselling services, or relevant external mental health resources, to employees and, where appropriate, to volunteers and Members experiencing mental health or wellbeing difficulties connected to their engagement with ISEA.

13.4 Right to Disconnect

ISEA supports reasonable boundaries between working and non-working time. Except where genuinely urgent or where an employee’s role requires otherwise, employees are not expected to routinely respond to work communications outside their normal working hours, having regard to time zone differences inherent in a global organisation.

13.5 Fatigue and Working Hours

ISEA recognises that fatigue arising from excessive working hours, insufficient rest, or extended international travel can impair judgement, increase the risk of error or incident, and adversely affect health. Managers should have regard to the cumulative effect of travel, event work and normal duties when scheduling employees and volunteers, and should take reasonable steps to ensure adequate rest periods, particularly around demanding events such as examinations and major conferences.

13.6 Support for New and Expectant Parents

ISEA will give reasonable consideration to the health and safety of employees who are pregnant, have recently given birth, or are returning to work after parental leave, including through appropriate risk assessment of their role and reasonable adjustments to duties, travel expectations or working arrangements where necessary, consistent with applicable local law.

Prevention of Workplace Violence, Aggression and Harassment

ISEA does not tolerate violence, threats, intimidation or aggressive conduct in its offices, at its events, or in connection with its activities. Conduct of this nature is addressed as a health and safety matter under this Policy and, where it involves harassment, bullying or victimisation related to a Protected Characteristic or otherwise, is addressed under ISEA’s Equality, Diversity and Inclusion Policy.

Where a person reasonably believes that they, or another person, are at risk of imminent harm, they should remove themselves from danger where safe to do so, seek assistance from venue security or local emergency services, and report the matter to ISEA as soon as reasonably practicable through the channels described in Section 17.

ISEA will take reasonable steps to assess and manage the risk of violence or aggression arising from identifiable circumstances, such as a contentious disciplinary matter, a distressed Applicant, or a known individual risk, and to protect employees and volunteers who may be exposed to such circumstances in the course of their role.

Alcohol, Substance Use and Event Safety

Alcohol may be served at certain ISEA social events and conference functions, consistent with applicable local law and professional norms. Where alcohol is served, ISEA expects attendees to consume it responsibly and expects hosts and event organisers to ensure that reasonable measures are in place, such as the availability of food and non-alcoholic beverages, and appropriate service standards consistent with venue and legal requirements.

The use of illegal drugs, or the misuse of alcohol or legal substances in a manner that impairs a person’s ability to safely perform their role or that endangers themselves or others, is not permitted in connection with any ISEA activity. Employees, volunteers and other individuals attending ISEA offices, examinations or events are expected not to attend, or to perform their role, while impaired by alcohol or a substance to an extent that compromises safety, professional conduct, or the integrity of an examination.

Concerns regarding a colleague’s or attendee’s apparent impairment should be raised promptly and sensitively with an ISEA staff member, event organiser or manager, having regard both to safety and to the wellbeing of the individual concerned.

First Aid and Medical Emergencies

ISEA will take reasonable steps to ensure that appropriate first aid provision is available at its offices and at significant ISEA-organised events, having regard to the size of the office or event, applicable local requirements, and the nature of the activities concerned.

First aid arrangements may include the appointment of trained first aiders among employees or event staff, the maintenance of appropriately stocked first aid kits, and clear signage or communication identifying first aid contacts and, where applicable, the location of automated external defibrillators.

In the event of a medical emergency, individuals should seek immediate assistance from local emergency services where appropriate, notify available first aiders or venue medical staff, and report the incident in accordance with Section 17 as soon as reasonably practicable thereafter.

Hazard and Incident Reporting

ISEA encourages the prompt reporting of hazards, incidents and near misses, in order to enable timely corrective action and to support continuous improvement in health, safety and wellbeing performance.

17.1 Who Should Report

Employees, volunteers, contractors, Members and event attendees are all encouraged to report hazards, incidents and near misses of which they become aware, whether or not they were personally affected.

17.2 How to Report

Reports may be made to a manager, event organiser, office administrator, the Executive Secretariat, or another designated health and safety contact identified at the relevant office or event. Serious incidents should be reported as soon as reasonably practicable and, in any event, before the person reporting leaves the office or event where safe and practicable to do so.

17.3 No Detriment for Good-Faith Reporting

ISEA will not subject any person to detriment for reporting, in good faith, a hazard, incident or health and safety concern under this Policy. This protection operates alongside, and is reinforced by, the protections available under ISEA’s Whistleblower Policy.

Incident Investigation and Corrective Action

ISEA will investigate reported incidents and near misses to a degree proportionate to their actual or potential severity, in order to understand the contributing causes and to identify appropriate corrective action.

ISEA’s incident investigation process is intended to:

establish the relevant facts and circumstances of the incident;

identify any immediate and underlying causes, including any failure of equipment, process or supervision;

identify corrective and preventive action to reduce the likelihood of recurrence; and

be conducted without attributing blame to any individual who reports an incident in good faith, consistent with Section 17.3.

Serious incidents, including those resulting in significant injury or requiring notification to a regulatory authority under applicable local law, shall be reported to the HSW Committee and, where appropriate, to the Governing Council.

Emergency Preparedness and Business Continuity

ISEA will maintain reasonable emergency preparedness arrangements for its offices and significant events, including emergency contact information, evacuation procedures, and, where appropriate to the size and risk profile of the office or activity, business continuity arrangements to maintain critical ISEA functions in the event of a significant disruption, such as a natural disaster, public health emergency, or significant security incident.

This Policy operates alongside ISEA’s Risk Management Policy in relation to broader organisational risk and business continuity planning, and the HSW Committee shall coordinate with the risk management function on matters of overlap.

Pandemic, Infectious Illness and Public Health Preparedness

Given the international nature of ISEA’s offices, conferences and examinations, ISEA recognises the importance of preparedness for pandemics, epidemics and other significant public health events that may affect its people, offices or events.

In relation to public health preparedness, ISEA will:

monitor relevant public health guidance issued by recognised national and international health authorities in the jurisdictions in which ISEA operates;

maintain the ability to adjust office working arrangements, such as remote working, in response to a significant public health event;

consider public health conditions as part of event risk assessments under Section 9.1, including, where appropriate, enhanced hygiene measures, capacity adjustments, or a decision to postpone, relocate or convert an event to a virtual or hybrid format; and

communicate clearly and promptly with employees, volunteers and Members regarding any public health measures affecting ISEA offices or events.

Employees, volunteers and attendees experiencing symptoms of a contagious illness are encouraged not to attend an ISEA office or event while contagious, consistent with any specific guidance issued for the relevant office or event, and consistent with applicable local law and any separate ISEA leave policies.

Occupational Health and Risk Assessment

ISEA will conduct risk assessments appropriate to its offices, events and operations, in order to identify hazards, evaluate risk, and determine appropriate control measures. Risk assessments shall be reviewed periodically and following any significant incident, change in premises, or material change in the nature of an activity.

21.1 Health Considerations for Specific Roles

Where an employee’s health condition may affect, or be affected by, their role, ISEA will, where reasonably practicable and with the employee’s consent, seek appropriate occupational health advice to inform any necessary workplace adjustments, consistent with the Reasonable Accommodation principles in ISEA’s Equality, Diversity and Inclusion Policy.

21.2 Fitness for Higher-Risk Activities

Where a specific ISEA-related activity carries a materially higher physical demand or risk, such as extended international travel to a demanding destination, ISEA may, where proportionate and consistent with applicable law, discuss Fitness for Role considerations with the individual concerned in order to identify any necessary support or adjustment, without requiring disclosure of a diagnosis or treating any disclosed health information other than in accordance with Section 23.

Training and Awareness

ISEA will provide health, safety and wellbeing training and information appropriate to the roles and activities of those to whom this Policy applies, including:

induction training for new employees, covering office safety, emergency procedures and incident reporting;

role-specific training for employees or volunteers undertaking higher-risk activities, such as event management or international travel;

periodic refresher training and awareness communications on topics such as mental health, ergonomics and emergency procedures; and

guidance materials for event organisers, chapter leaders and volunteers on event and travel safety expectations.

Managers are responsible for ensuring that employees and contractors within their area of responsibility complete health and safety training relevant to their role.

Health, Safety and Wellbeing Records and Privacy

Information relating to incidents, hazards, risk assessments and health and safety or wellbeing concerns will be recorded and retained in accordance with ISEA’s Document Retention Policy, and will be handled with appropriate confidentiality, disclosed only to those persons who reasonably need to know it in order to investigate and address the matter, ensure compliance with applicable law, or fulfil ISEA’s duty of care.

Personal information, including health-related information, collected in connection with this Policy will be processed in accordance with ISEA’s Privacy Policy and applicable data protection law, and will be used only for the purposes of managing health, safety and wellbeing, unless the individual concerned consents to a further use or disclosure is otherwise required by law.
